The importance of the 2026 election is obvious. A dictatorial president subverting the Constitution to gain more power for himself while Congress stands by in thrall, subservient to his political movement. November may be our last chance to stand and defend our democracy and our elections.
Pitch in $35 -- right now -- to fuel our efforts to inform eligible voters, get them registered, get their ballot cast, and make every vote count >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=071926_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
When it comes to fighting voter suppression, our work is never done. Increasing participation in free and fair elections that are accessible to ALL eligible voters is our #1 goal for 2026, Team.
Unfortunately, this is what we're facing as we start the year:
➜ Mail-in voting is under threat in state legislatures and now from the Supreme Court.
➜ Without vote-by-mail, millions of Americans will not be able to vote.
➜ With the 2026 midterm election around the corner, this is a disaster.
Remember, Team: Attacks on mail-in voting are voter suppression, plain and simple. We need your help now, more than ever. Will you chip in $35 to protect vote-by-mail before it’s too late? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=071926_3&amount=35]

These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

Jensen Huang said they’ll “continue to support _this firm_ for decades to come.”

But NVIDIA isn’t the only one who needs it.

Elon Musk’s SpaceX builds on it — their job postings demand experience with this firm’s technology, in writing.

Jeff Bezos builds Amazon’s AI chips on it, and Blue Origin runs its control systems on it. Apple, Google, Meta, Samsung, and Qualcomm all pay it billions in royalties every year.

Its technology is already in the phone in your hand.

Every time you open an app, stream a video, or ask your assistant a question, [_this company’s_](https://links.notify.powerfieldnotes.com/u/click?_t=e11a13a19fbf4d1ab3d90eea26ea896f&_m=3e424b3752314259bdcce6f9ec917c05&_e=Nbmz3bjXx_uhaHDCpMeVhrUy4waW2ONkQ99IGCFgszfWLPdEQMCTemFj2sjmLoTEdA6GHTxctF-kXtkueAjTacGBDD0DXmr6gsHP1l92adIRTgwsJjuR3v22Ia3dgZGQO3Ayr96G7DLP5CC9mXMt4E0NeJsNcBfL5C2EuYydJDuNMUOTdiozgzlodaTFt46-rddzbbSOJJvCpBPi9saVqyY6zF6Frtwroqs-3-RHbswRFIT0Dhhrl0p0cuVI63eE-PMKq6O2o6uvxRHlJtUGaFe3T5gbIX2tSiqelEqUnx0Sy-rjG9YUmT_4zHUJJVWmC1pxneeB5vmwaGwIxAEAc3zoRiTPzZeddx3RtO-iQlUDFeUvSnXlGAJhSTPMuaqgziDMIxpCl49J6ZZG6WQgxq1V_7xpCERG5NmngDl72ko9_67bGPRzwLmp9r82omk3LCQ7bImCkMa7BgC_s09hqWm7aYQZrz72Ae3sMRDIWw4%3D) architecture is running underneath.

| | **Q2 2026 Was the Worst Quarter for Oil Markets Since COVID. US Petroleum Markets Are the Story. Iranian Power Infrastructure Is Now a Casualty. Here Is the Week's Full Accounting.**
---
| | EIA's Today in Energy documented Q2 2026 petroleum markets: they were "characterized by continued disruptions to international crude oil and petroleum product flows through the Strait of Hormuz, contributing to higher and more volatile crude oil prices through most of the quarter." International buyers sought alternative supply sources for petroleum products — directly driving up US petroleum product exports to record levels. Cushing, Oklahoma storage — the delivery point for WTI futures — fell below 20 million barrels during the week ending June 19 through July 10, the lowest sustained inventory in years. The EIA's July indicator table puts the full picture in one row: Brent spot averaged $82/barrel in 2026 in their forecast versus $69 in 2025 — a $13/barrel average increase for the year, representing the largest annual crude price increase since 2021-2022.
---
| | Iran's Energy Ministry called on Iranians this week to limit air conditioning use after US strikes damaged power lines near Bandar Abbas, causing electricity supply disruptions in southern Iran, per CNN. This is the first documented case in the conflict of US strikes directly degrading a civilian electricity supply system. Trump threatened in his national address to strike Iranian "electric generating plants" if Iran does not negotiate — which would be a far more complete destruction of civilian power infrastructure than the incidental damage that has already occurred. Iran processes approximately 90% of its oil exports through Kharg Island; it generates significant electricity from natural gas infrastructure in the south. Targeting either at full scale would cause cascading civilian harm that humanitarian law experts say constitutes a war crime. The line between military infrastructure and civilian power in Iran's case is thin. The strikes are moving closer to it.

Dear Friends,I wanted you to be among the first to hear the news—I am excited to announce that I’m running for Daly City Council!This campaign is built on one simple principle: local government should provide **opportunity for all.** Today, families across our city are feeling the squeeze of rising housing, healthcare, and grocery costs. Young families wonder if they can afford to stay, and seniors worry about being priced out. Working people deserve a City Hall focused on making life more affordable while protecting the unique quality of life that makes Daly City so special.As a lifelong resident and the proud son of working-class Filipino immigrants, these challenges are personal. My family has called Daly City home since 1977, when my parents bought our home at the Top of the Hill. I attended our local schools and learned the values of hard work, service, and looking out for your neighbors.My career has been dedicated to serving this community. For the past ten years, I’ve served as Chief of Staff to San Mateo County Supervisor David J. Canepa. As Vice Chair of Daly City's Personnel Board, I’ve also gained firsthand experience in making local government more responsive and accountable. I know how to navigate government, build partnerships, and bring resources home because I’ve spent my career doing exactly that.If elected, I will focus on delivering real results that provides opportunity for all:
* **Affordability:** Improving housing affordability, expanding healthcare access, and helping families keep up with the cost of living.
* **Public Safety & Infrastructure:** Investing in first responders, fixing flooding challenges, repairing potholes, and strengthening transit options.
* **Family Support:** Advocating for a childcare center at Daly City Hall to support working parents and make city services more accessible.
* **Senior Care:** Protecting and expanding programs that help seniors age safely and independently in their homes.

**I’m ready to step into a leadership role myself in every way but I can’t do it without you. As I know from helping to run Supervisor Canepa’s campaigns and you probably do too, campaigns are not cheap.**[**Can you be one of my founding donors?**](https://us.list-manage.com/AKOXwIpqEUE?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)**Nothing is more important to a campaign than early money, as it helps us get off to a fast start and build a winning campaign from the get-go.**
[**Could you donate today in any amount up to $5,900? $1,000, $500, $100 or even $25 will make a huge difference to my campaign at this early stage.**](https://us.list-manage.com/9O8DEOWxsMt?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)
Our city has always been defined by hardworking families, diverse neighborhoods, and neighbors who care about one another. Together, we can build a Daly City that is more affordable, safer, better prepared for the future, and continues to be a place where families of every generation can thrive – a Daly City that truly provides opportunity for all.I would be honored to earn your support, your ideas, and your vote.In friendship,
Tony BayudanCandidate for Daly City Council**P.S. Anything you can donate today at**[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tony-bayudan-1**](https://us.list-manage.com/17nY9h13TgY?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)**will be so valuable – even if it’s just $5!**

Sustainer Sunday
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260719-3054)
Peter,
Every Sunday, we share the story of someone who's helping build this movement and why they believe Fran is the leader Wisconsin needs.
Earlier this year, Fran earned an endorsement from [Black Leaders Organizing for Communities (BLOC)](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16816?t=1&akid=3054%2E105371%2ESDLgXR), the powerhouse grassroots organization that organizes year-round in Milwaukee's Black communities.
Today, we're hearing from Angela Lang, BLOC's founder and executive director, on why she’s backing Fran.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260719.6pD6zH&refcode=em20260719-3054&t=2&akid=3054%2E105371%2ESDLgXR)
* * *
_Fran has been authentically showing up in our communities for years, not just when she is running for office._
_She doesn’t shy away from tough conversations. She listens, speaks honestly and is committed to being accountable to the people she serves._
_Wisconsinites have been waiting for leaders willing to challenge a status quo that has failed working people for far too long._
_Fran understands that real change begins by listening to the people most affected and then having the courage to fight alongside them._
_\- Angela Lang, Milwaukee_
* * *
Angela’s testimonial reflects what this campaign hears every day across Wisconsin: People are ready for leadership that does not take their communities for granted.
Trust can't be bought – not with corporate PAC money, not with a billionaire's checkbook. It's earned door by door, block by block, conversation by conversation. That's how Fran has run this campaign, and it's how she'll lead as governor. But out-organizing candidates with establishment backing takes resources.
**We’re working harder than ever to reach voters before the Aug. 11 primary.**

With gratitude,
Team Hong

subject: I brought my son to the auto shop because we couldn't find childcare
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY MGP VICTORY FUND, A JOINT
body:

Before I was sworn into Congress, my husband and I brought our son to our auto repair shop most days.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
Not because it was cute. Because there was no other option.
There wasn't a daycare within a reasonable drive, and the care we could find cost more than we could afford. So he came to work with us — in a shop full of lifts and tools — because that was the choice in front of us.
We are not unusual. That's the reality for working parents across Southwest Washington, especially in our rural communities, where you can drive an hour and still not find an open spot.
Here's something almost no one in DC will say out loud: out of 535 members of Congress, only six of the women have a child under six. I'm one of them. Most of the people writing childcare policy haven't had to find a daycare spot — or afford one — in decades. I still do.
I didn't need a briefing to understand this problem. I lived it.
That's why I introduced the Expanding Childcare in Rural America Act . And it's why I spent three years on something so basic it sounds made up: in Washington State, red tape makes it easier for a home daycare to hand a kid a processed, packaged snack than to peel a banana or cut up an apple.
This spring, the House finally passed my bill to cut that red tape. It's a small thing that makes smaller daycares stay afloat, which are lifelines for working families.
That's the work I came here to do: fixing the specific, stupid problems that make it harder to raise a family and earn a living.
But I'm one of the most targeted Democrats in the country, in one of the closest districts in America. Donald Trump has endorsed my opponent, and national Republicans will spend whatever it takes to take this seat back.
Will you chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can to keep this campaign going? Every dollar helps us reach one more working parent who's tired of being told their problems aren't worth solving. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
Thank you for standing with me.
—Marie

Friends [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50] ,
Right now, so much of what’s going on feels hard. And if you’re anything like me, there are far too many things keeping you up at night. That’s our reality right now, and I’m not going to write you an email pretending everything is all sunshine and rainbows.
I’ve also been thinking a lot lately about the fights ahead, and about how important it is to make time for the things that bring us joy. Even in the middle of all of this — or rather, especially in the middle of all of this!
I’m a proud aunt, and I take aunt-ing very seriously — to the point of reading toddler blogs in my spare time. One of the main takeaways from the blogs I follow is that you can't pour from an empty cup . In other words, if we're going to keep showing up as the best version of ourselves (whether as an aunt, a friend, a Congresswoman, or whatever else life brings), we have to take care of ourselves first.
I took a few days off recently for the first time in a very long time — and if you’re in the position to do the same, I hope you will. But at the very least, consider this email your reminder to make time for yourself in small ways: Move your body. Cook something delicious. Get some sunshine. Play pickleball (my personal stress reliever). Go for a walk. Listen to a podcast. Read a book!
And if you're looking for something to read, I've got some recommendations. Here are some of my favorites from this summer:
Into the Blue by Emma Brodie — 9/10. A little weird, but it kept my attention and had some great plot twists.
The Night We Met by Abby Jimenez — 8/10. The perfect light beach read. Very sweet.
Traitor to His Class by H.W. Brands — 9/10. OK, this is a biography of FDR that somehow isn't boring at all. Full of fascinating details — like the fact that his mother Sara's (a fellow no-H Sara!) family is from New Bedford, just like mine.
The Shippers by Katherine Center — 8/10. Perfectly light and cute.
And honestly, anything by Emily Henry, because you can't go wrong!
If you’re reading something good right now, I'd love to hear about it — so please reply to this email and tell me what you’re enjoying, or what’s in your to-be-read pile. I'm always looking for my next book.
Take care of yourselves. We need you in this fight for the long haul!
—Sara

A Democrat has controlled the Kansas Governor's office since 2019 and experts believe Democrats have a strong shot at capturing it again this November. As such we've had control over this supreme court's nomination process for longer than half a decade.

Under their ballot measure, judicial elections will be presided over by the GOP controlled Kansas legislature -- this way they will be able to rig them and ensure their candidates win.

In 2019 the Kansas Supreme Court ruled to recognize the right to abortion in the state's Constitution, in 2022 MAGA pushed a ballot measure to overturn this but in a move that shocked the nation voters rejected it. Now, on August 4th, 2026, in Kansas's upcoming statewide primary election, MAGA has what could be their last chance to criminalize abortion here. | == On the ballot for Kansas's upcoming election is an obscure measure that will decide whether the state should elect its state's supreme court judges, or if they should stick with the status quo where the governor appoints justices to the court. A Democrat has controlled the Kansas Governor's office since 2019 and experts believe Democrats have a strong shot at capturing it again this November. As such we've had control over this supreme court's nomination process for longer than half a decade. MAGA knows they may never win the Governor's office again so they hope to change the system and elect judges as opposed to appointing them. Under their ballot measure, judicial elections will be presided over by the GOP controlled Kansas legislature -- this way they will be able to rig them and ensure their candidates win. A win for MAGA on this critical ballot issue could mean that Kansans could be stripped of their right to abortion by the end of 2027. Peter,
Democrats' chances of flipping the Senate this election took a massive hit:
Graham Platner, the Democratic nominee in Maine, going up against Sen. Susan Collins, just imploded after credible and disturbing allegations were made against him.
Platner has finally dropped out of the race, but Maine Democrats will now have to navigate uncharted waters to select a new nominee to take Platner's place on the ballot.
Meanwhile, Susan Collins has over $10 million in her campaign war chest and near-unlimited spending from MAGA groups waiting to ambush whoever the party nominates.

We're not going to sugarcoat it: While we are confident Maine Democrats can still pull this off, we need to ensure Democrats' have multiple paths to winning back the US Senate in November.
But all is not lost for our hopes of flipping the Senate and reining in Trump this midterm -- far from it.
Nebraska is emerging as Democrats' best remaining hope to win the Senate this year: billionaire MAGA Senator Pete Ricketts is on the ropes, and every single poll (both public and private polling) shows him statistically tied with his main opponent, Dan Osborn.
With Maine up in the air, the path to reclaiming control of the Senate this November requires a win in Nebraska.
And while we can be justifiably angry and disgusted at the Platner campaign's deceptive tactics that have put our chances of unseating Susan Collins in jeopardy, we also must focus on figuring out the best way forward.
Democrats have a once-in-a-lifetime chance to flip Nebraska in November \- but we can't do it if we don't double down right now to defeat Pete Ricketts and take the Senate majority away from Republicans.

## Spain Beats Argentina 1-0 for World Cup Title
Spain's Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute to lift his country to a [1-0 victory over Argentina](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAQRL_Gzhg1PQzYAcElm-2lF1o90B73CYMF7Fr79yfPL1xWpZJK9erP5_JJkiS_ftPOvq9lyXy2xL1zXdpBkk_J7Sw1hq-jndLDxpEWBLQKnEJYIkn6WcwY_cqMfB_ZazeZh9EzmnHzpIFWi9P0vGtDFpF1XHUE1BaDm2kUf7WBQ9AAD9Q31pMJOEd4kHYTPAYDHKWXevtbJPeN1_RTvrneQtnH5Lfejzbcfw34MeAHHRfAFV2mdgmJ3-rFuUsm9YZSZ6kpqvB1qFUyJdVCqax2bk3UGkJAS6QxzoiW7T2CfVrQT-fAajdWH49TUpJm3WDgtZOk95j-Xw9-e_wXAAD__10vg_o) and its second World Cup title. The dramatic finish capped a record-setting FIFA World Cup that drew more than 6.6 million fans to 16 stadiums across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico. Argentina was reduced to 10 men in stoppage time at the end of regulation when Enzo Fernández received his second yellow card. ---
| | Brent crude rose 3% Sunday to $90.78 per barrel — its highest level since the April 2026 war peak — after the US struck nine Iranian cities in its ninth consecutive night of operations and Iran hit the Jordanian city of Aqaba. WTI crude is now up 24.89% year-on-year, per Trading Economics. The EIA's July STEO, completed July 1, forecast Q3 2026 Brent at $74/barrel and US retail gasoline at $3.80/gallon — both numbers written when the MOU was intact and the Strait was reopening. That document is now $16.78/barrel below the current Brent spot price. Every $10 rise in Brent adds roughly 24 cents per gallon to retail gasoline. The $16.78 gap between the EIA Q3 forecast and today's Brent price translates to approximately 40 cents per gallon in additional pump cost over the July forecast baseline — bringing the implied Q3 gasoline price to approximately $4.20/gallon or higher if Brent remains elevated. With Brent at $90+, $4.50 is realistic.
---
| | The IEA's July OMR confirmed global oil supply rebounded by 4.1 mb/d to 98.8 mb/d in June as the ceasefire briefly reopened the Strait — but noted world output remains 9.4 mb/d below pre-war levels, with supply on track to fall 3.7 mb/d in 2026 overall. That rebound is now reversing. The Strait has dropped to three vessels per day. Nine Iranian cities were struck overnight. Iran fired toward the Israeli border. The 4.1 mb/d June rebound was the MOU working for three weeks. The MOU is voided. The August 11 EIA STEO is the next document that will attempt to price this. It will be written against a backdrop of: three dead Americans, nine struck cities, Brent at $90+, a nuclear window with 28 days left, and a Houthi standby order on the last viable bypass route. That is an energy market document nobody in July would have chosen to write.

## Trump Approves Flood Emergency Declaration
President Donald Trump approved a [federal emergency declaration](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQxvGngc3IHDYmg4cubOnaERl8hpMMRuYSkj59lQxV9-6nv-73fV2Hq6NI2_zpVrT8CGnY8DwiMmMecMU84zY9PU7RZceUNrfvOQ0goRXSCJCDdxSfgyq9HaW_1CXa2nRKK90oXS62Ud0olUclpWp1M3bjOHYGTTCXFgxASfYVkwZkXUuAutJ46WqtO98qPaHWhZLoiVOueEHGhztCfKY75mpKaxntwrwfRfNRQF9Af55nFdLDuNvBtL1OCuhfpgJ6zrd1F2_BHQ_xbokQU_Lilyr-WIW78ZIyfdM2i4CrExkjYSiz9ftJMdLRmkLJeXUU39_w_za8W_gJAAD__134iSw) for 28 flood-stricken Texas counties on Saturday, authorizing FEMA to coordinate disaster relief. The declaration covers counties across South and Central Texas--including Bexar, Kerr, Comal, Bandera, and Uvalde--hit by flooding that began July 12. The federal government will reimburse 75% of eligible emergency response costs, including search and rescue and emergency medical care. Gov. Greg Abbott signed a [disaster declaration Friday in Uvalde,](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAUhZ8Gb0RwDSYeGLqwpWtHi5ibmAobBDd_b1856tC98zn6dM73dZpOPqa4XT_9ipaelzxt-GgJibBOuGK94ja_As7JV08xb76UmicQMHBhOIgp-Jhek-qCPYswyg6tNEelle6V7har0ffqrKSSug_hPJpBX7TqjRI-GBiHLtodJgwIKQWAPGgcj1LrYxiUnlFrpgSGSLkeaEHCp2-X9Mp3rIc5r12yC1FprP9g4Bi4VnCmeltTnn3av-wtBo6ee5hvtPA3g2PixbfMwO0tBm6fwcAJw8DJkYErFVsMuBHfgYW_r9-x_QL46r9z5SE23wgr_yOpqzaUR0wptsEwJa6rj-k9l_4n-W7hJwAA___jd5I2) requesting federal aid. He said the [state had deployed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb_G7rAwAdsUFNu4y7ZbWs_wiNFisOAlTubrR0kxPzD1vffo6vy7LlcIMaTbX9jR0NPnJeFZIxJhWXDHcsNkXw5thAIUcoLjKHkRXAyMj0zwxUGIr0W2zqzc6b5F04-TVFJdpGo342HV2jmQ6PXI3XiRvld2UOs6cS61boN5w_goeN9zIfpOoZ56pSY3SGVRqUZydIFy6WhDwidUH1_5gaWzeW-j2YiO2lz-NGJuxHyeZ_f_CekdNmK2mKhAZJ9dI-ajYA0OEzEq9_1gcKctl_CFlXl0-K4WjAE9g1pDJUgWmc_lB9AW444zxBjqMDaS33YI8fOEfufvYcR3AAAA___cN4fL) more than 2,700 personnel, 90 boats, and 20 aircraft to rescue more than 270 people. FEMA said additional assistance could be approved if damage assessments show more federal aid is warranted.
## Flooding Forces Camp Eagle Evacuation
State troopers and [volunteer firefighters evacuated](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkMGupCAQRb9Gd3QAQX0LFrNx92Y7S1NAoSRIGWC627-ftJk_eNuTk6qT--d7_YaYYt5-w4GmvQOtGV81YWtYVjywbJjd5dElKNAiZTjPQqvkcmR8YpKvHmK6VtV7Y7n_Ej0aMc1KKz0o3e-Gz24KdrDDJEZuvbc2DGIcZ2uFD4MLfTSfY3ySXAgupXho_JqF1rMflXaodac4-tioPNqODd9QQ7roieXh6OiT2Vs7azf86uTSyeWTrypkyI1ypI_zn3ZySeQgdXI5d2pU2SA1c3CcWCrDJ7i_0NCzUOi4MUPYEjJ7sfsr82dlrRDdPhzRs5CIfMxbX4w_XzGlWMepU3w7IKY7r_1s1KeR_wIAAP__QIePNg) about 325 campers from Camp Eagle in Real County on Saturday after flooding washed out the camp's main access road. The Texas Department of Public Safety said Real County Judge Bella Rubio requested the evacuation and that [every camper made it out safely](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGu4yAQRb8Gd0R4DBgKim3cvW23tCYwidFiYwEvTv5-5WT_4JX3zOhIV_fP1_yFMcXt_htXcu15y_NGR03UGpWZVip32vwrkE9YsMW84b6XPIMAzcXIQcwBY3rNsgvuKoLtO3L9aKSSapCqW5wBYwxKsIrIWgDptbyq0atee2-BuuhOmRhB9L0A6C-KrOmVMkFL5UkpJgWF2HK5tIUaPbHe0is_qFx8Xrvkltb2yoZfDCYG03Ecl7-0VXVeGUxYWvSJGExnMQZTbdjO-Dbx__ATbinnwGAahOAf4nHdqVROD_Tf2Ci8CSe8J_q88wPrQpXn78bRe6qVl4ynBcaBYxjNYPXApbGaSyTgxmrFvRTXISh9pZvqigv7EVOKVY9MivuKMb27tZ8t8nDwLwAA__8kG54B). Troopers from the DPS South Texas Region worked alongside the Center Point Volunteer Fire Department and local partners. Amphibious SHERP vehicles—one donated to the Center Point firefighters [by Joe Rogan and Ron White](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLtuxCAURL8Gd6wAgx8FRRp3mzaldQ3XNtE1WMC-_j7a5BPSjTTSaM75us5XCBTi9gkH2vpc0xzxUQhrxTzjgXnD6F4eHUGGGlKE88xpVkJ1XPRcidlDoNesG28X4UfZoJX9oI02rTbNbgE6LZxbdIdSo2jHflickqMbhWzXXjXBvsdEr4SUQil5MTgO0pjBd9o4NIZpgT7UlC91x4pPKCu90h3zxaWjIbvXehbWfjA1MTW5pcCt1BDfLVPTG4epiZIDYmr6Tshz2iBynyJU9LzsmE9-xz04Qr4jneh5xuJuyB0cJ0fY6C9iLnxNROkR4sZXSsmHuDXZ-vMRiELpeqbFdkCg32_1f0bvVv0EAAD__8syjb4)—carried campers over the washed-out terrain to buses waiting at the highway. State Rep. Wes Virdell said the campers were never in danger during the severe weather.
## Boxer Hannah Rapp Killed in Crash
Rising professional boxer Hannah "Hanarchy" Rapp, 26, died Saturday after a driver struck her [while she was cycling](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OhCAUxfGnwQ7Dh6hTUGxjN9tuaa5wHcggEGRH3affzL7C1if55eT_dZ_v4IOPj0_YUNdzTXPEYw9YK5YZNywPjOayaAIUqD5FyLmkWTDRUzZQwWYLPlxz11i9MHvjDWo-jJ3qlOxU4_QKduQrjsb0Bq1kbJQS1SpVL-WietZ4_cbYIBjnTAjeKryNXKnR9p0yqBTpGFpfU2mrw4on7Gu40gtLa9LWBO1qzTuRH0RMREzHcbTPpZ7vkYjpbRMxsYGIid-ImBzECI46iFCMu2iBnKlxsGWfIl3SiYU-fQho6VLgJ-3UpO9YL2oK7I6IqSna5sOH4Pd-IB17bODD35X6v4AvLX4DAAD__0MIhOg) on FM 159 in Brazos County. The Brazos County Sheriff's Office said Charles Medina, 31, of Navasota, passed Rapp and another cyclist at a high rate of speed, then braked, reversed, [and accelerated backward](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD0O3CAQRk-DO1YwNv4pKNK427QprVmYNSgYLDxZr28fOVdI9RVPevr0fj2XJ8YU8_oTN7L8fZcl03kkYqa60EZ1pewuTy5hRY4l477XsoCCXqpBglo8xnQtXePtS_lJN2T1MHamM21nmmBbPTnnCLwZ27ebjOv7qX05eI2da1G_m2hvmRpAaa0A9MPQNGpjRt93xpExolPkI5f64EBMXzze6Sofqg9XtibZwLwfov0hYBYwn-f5-H3y94YC5tstYFaDgFlPAuaMHzwKo9wwS6yVDiYvXcC6kpdn5HCTI-GfNTBV6Qk5yFf5UpUBc8ZwD1YXLllx3wXMTbV-P2NK8egH0al1w5j-neP_S_qx8DcAAP__UyWMEg) into her. Medina was charged with manslaughter and is held on a $250,000 bond. Investigators wrote that skid marks and the severity of the vehicle damage contradicted Medina's account that he was backing up slowly. Jail records show it was his 13th booking in Brazos County since 2012. Rapp moved from Indiana to Bryan-College Station about two years ago and fought for a WBC [featherweight world title](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpSAYhZ8GOwwgKLeg2MbubrulAflRsigG_7no20-cV5jmFOckX06-f-_pbWOK-_LXbmDwCnnaoZ4JEKFMsEFZYJ9vD3OyxWLMuz2OkifBRE_ZQAWbvI3pnmTjjWP-xRswfNBSSdVJ1awmBBBBBjvrXmvdyQH6wHsO0jvphqCbaB4YGwTjnAnBWwUvzZXSvpdqBqWIZOAj5tLiCgiXPUO68wdKO-etSWZFPE7S_SFiJGKstbb_HV7PSMT4sIkY2RO8I2J05bY7dfmCQkNcVoz7QqubaQCLK5QKT0lrLslTjJiAnha_irc3EWNTjD9qTCme_UAkWzYb088P_J29jxHfAQAA__8X7IRQ) in June, all while working full-time at Texas A&M.

The Brazos County Sheriff's Office said Charles Medina, 31, of Navasota, passed Rapp and another cyclist at a high rate of speed, then braked, reversed, into her. I got a phone call from a candidate for Governor in a Midwestern state yesterday. We are friendly, but he's a current candidate, so this wasn't a social call. I cut to the chase:
"Hey, I know you're in the midst of a campaign. What can I do to help?"
"Well, we have a fundraising deadline this week and want to put up a good number. Thank you for already donating to my campaign. Could you donate even more?"
"Sure," I said. "Happy to help."
"Great," he said. "I'll send you a link."
The entire call took maybe 2 minutes. I try to be very fast with these calls because it's a gift for the candidate to get their time back.
I would know, as I made hundreds or even thousands of those calls when I was running for President. It's hard to keep track. Whenever you're in a rental vehicle for more than 30 minutes, a staffer says, "Great, we can do call time!" And then your soul recoils.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/65449972-a8bd-4057-a9ee-715ca9904793?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I hated doing call time. I would much rather do what a normal person does in the car - listen to music or have a conversation. Or even check and post on social media, which was sort of a hybrid move because it theoretically drove value to the campaign and also didn't make you want to shoot yourself on a good day.
As someone who has made so many of these calls, I try to be the ideal recipient. Fast, supportive, efficient, and no hoop-jumping. No questions from me. No advice. Just deliver value and be encouraging.
"I was a bit naive when I ran in 2022," said [Brian Bengs](https://substack.com/redirect/77614317-6fb1-4f98-a5c5-88ec9711aa95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who is currently running for Senator in South Dakota as an Independent. "I went out to people in diners and flea markets telling them who I was and why I was running as an antidote to politics-as-usual. Kind of an old-fashioned vision of campaigning. South Dakota only has 935,000 people so I could theoretically get in front of a decent percentage of voters." It probably helps that Brian, an Air Force veteran and former college instructor, is 6' 8" tall and sticks out in a crowd.
"This time, in 2026 I'm spending a lot more time on the phone doing call time," Brian continues. "I've realized that the money matters more than we like to admit. My campaign has raised more money this year than any non-incumbent in 12 years. I still get out in front of people but more so on weekends when folks get together." That rhythm was familiar to me. "South Dakota is a very cheap state to advertise in, so having raised almost a million dollars is a very big deal here." Brian is polling within 4 points of the 71-year-old incumbent, Mike Rounds, in a one-on-one race in a state that Trump won by 29% in 2024. It's another reminder that Americans want more choices beyond the usual red versus blue. I donated to Brian's campaign gladly as a high-leverage opportunity.
I admire folks like Brian who are on the campaign trail. He's working hard. As a candidate, you put yourself out there and do what you have to do. When I made those phone calls, a good productive call would sometimes energize me for the next one. Still, in my case I immediately hungered to graduate from call time to something that felt more like movement-building, from one-to-one to one-to-many.
I've belatedly learned, though, that you probably never really graduate. Obama wound up having to make phone calls for his newly opened presidential center with much higher dollar amounts attached. I still call people. The best you can hope for is that you have the right people calling for the right reasons, or, if you're the one making the calls, that people actually pick up. An end to dialing-for-dollars would make my heart sing.
I hope you're enjoying the summer! For my conversation with [Brian Bengs](https://substack.com/redirect/77614317-6fb1-4f98-a5c5-88ec9711aa95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), U.S. Senate candidate for South Dakota, click [here](https://substack.com/redirect/19dea981-0bbf-4f6d-99ba-68b47809c2ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). clean_body: I got a phone call from a candidate for Governor in a Midwestern state yesterday. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | ---|---|--- * | | | Jul 20 | | | | | | | | | | | | I got a phone call from a candidate for Governor in a Midwestern state yesterday. We are friendly, but he's a current candidate, so this wasn't a social call. I cut to the chase: "Hey, I know you're in the midst of a campaign. What can I do to help?" "Well, we have a fundraising deadline this week and want to put up a good number. Thank you for already donating to my campaign. Could you donate even more?" "Sure," I said. "Happy to help." "Great," he said. "I'll send you a link." The entire call took maybe 2 minutes. I try to be very fast with these calls because it's a gift for the candidate to get their time back. I would know, as I made hundreds or even thousands of those calls when I was running for President. It's hard to keep track. Whenever you're in a rental vehicle for more than 30 minutes, a staffer says, "Great, we can do call time!" And then your soul recoils. | | ---|---|--- I hated doing call time. I would much rather do what a normal person does in the car - listen to music or have a conversation. Or even check and post on social media, which was sort of a hybrid move because it theoretically drove value to the campaign and also didn't make you want to shoot yourself on a good day. As someone who has made so many of these calls, I try to be the ideal recipient. Fast, supportive, efficient, and no hoop-jumping. No questions from me. No advice. Just deliver value and be encouraging. "I was a bit naive when I ran in 2022," said , who is currently running for Senator in South Dakota as an Independent. "I went out to people in diners and flea markets telling them who I was and why I was running as an antidote to politics-as-usual. Kind of an old-fashioned vision of campaigning. South Dakota only has 935,000 people so I could theoretically get in front of a decent percentage of voters." It probably helps that Brian, an Air Force veteran and former college instructor, is 6' 8" tall and sticks out in a crowd. "This time, in 2026 I'm spending a lot more time on the phone doing call time," Brian continues. "I've realized that the money matters more than we like to admit. My campaign has raised more money this year than any non-incumbent in 12 years. I still get out in front of people but more so on weekends when folks get together." That rhythm was familiar to me. "South Dakota is a very cheap state to advertise in, so having raised almost a million dollars is a very big deal here." Brian is polling within 4 points of the 71-year-old incumbent, Mike Rounds, in a one-on-one race in a state that Trump won by 29% in 2024. It's another reminder that Americans want more choices beyond the usual red versus blue. I donated to Brian's campaign gladly as a high-leverage opportunity. I admire folks like Brian who are on the campaign trail. He's working hard. As a candidate, you put yourself out there and do what you have to do. When I made those phone calls, a good productive call would sometimes energize me for the next one. Still, in my case I immediately hungered to graduate from call time to something that felt more like movement-building, from one-to-one to one-to-many. I've belatedly learned, though, that you probably never really graduate. Obama wound up having to make phone calls for his newly opened presidential center with much higher dollar amounts attached. I still call people. The best you can hope for is that you have the right people calling for the right reasons, or, if you're the one making the calls, that people actually pick up. An end to dialing-for-dollars would make my heart sing. I hope you're enjoying the summer! For my conversation with , U.S. Senate candidate for South Dakota, click . I'm doing a book this Wednesday in LA on July 22nd. For 3 months off your mobile bill with Noble Mobile, click or email and use my name to switch or explore. * * *
#### On Thursday, July 16th, a company most Americans have never heard of released an artificial intelligence model that caught the American frontier lab models, and it released it from Beijing.
The company is called Moonshot AI. The model is Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, the largest model ever slated for open release, and within hours of its debut it stood in first place on Arena's Frontend Code leaderboard, ahead of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, the two most capable systems the American labs have ever shipped--first, in fact, in six of the seven coding categories. On Arena's broader text rankings it finished ahead of Claude Opus 4.8, Anthropic's flagship until five weeks ago, while costing 40 percent less to run.
And on Monday, July 27th, Moonshot says, it will give the whole thing away: the weights, the architecture, everything, free to download and free to run in any data center on earth. **The weights are the model itself, the billions of numbers in which everything it learned is stored; whoever holds them holds the machine.**
**Moonshot --and, by extension, China, just beat us at AI and is giving the model away. For FREE.**
Axios said it plainly Friday morning: "China just erased America's AI lead."
Eighty years to build, and all it took was one random Thursday to lose.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a931ddae-8b64-4d60-a985-a52f72847ce0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Beijing, China
* * *
#### **The computer is an American invention.**
The theory owes a debt to a British mathematician, Turing, who his own government hounded to death, but the machines--the actual, humming, room-filling, world-changing machines--were built here in the United States.
In February 1946, in a room at the University of Pennsylvania, engineers threw the switches on ENIAC, thirty tons of vacuum tubes and hand-soldered wire that could do in thirty seconds what a human being with a desk calculator needed twenty hours to finish. The transistor came out of Bell Labs in New Jersey the following year; the integrated circuit out of Texas and California a decade after that; the microprocessor out of Santa Clara in 1971.
The supercomputer was substantially the work of one stubborn man in Chippewa Falls, Wisconsin--Seymour Cray, who treated speed as a calling. The internet began as ARPANET, a Pentagon research project that spoke its first halting word between UCLA and the Stanford Research Institute in the autumn of 1969. And the transformer architecture that makes every modern AI model possible--Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and yes, Kimi K3--was published in 2017 by eight researchers at Google, in a paper the company let out the door for free.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a931ddae-8b64-4d60-a985-a52f72847ce0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
ENIAC
Every layer of this revolution was laid down on American ground, much of it with public money, much of it by people who came here from somewhere else because here was where you came to build. The record reads like myth and is footnoted like history. Computing is the American inheritance the way navigation belonged to Portugal and steel belonged to Sheffield, except bigger, because computing became the substrate everything else now runs on--including steel manufacturing and navigation.
I am not a neutral witness to any of this. I spent twenty-five years inside the American tech industry, managing programs at the largest scale it had to offer, and I believed--actually believed, the way you believe things at two in the morning in a war room when the release finally goes green--that we were building the future for everyone.
Then the industry decided that people my age were a cost center, the first wave of this technology arrived to absorb our work, and I got to experience the American way of implementing AI from the receiving end.
**I know what these companies are from the inside, which is why you should believe me when I tell you: this was the home game, the one field we were supposed to lose last, or never at all.**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.KP0_3w9XppfYE4hsl0wbmvjlGkGZaryZBRasJ1jqQBU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=207582150)
* * *
#### In 2023, the men running America's AI industry told us China was eighteen months behind, and eighteen months, at frontier speed, was forever.
By last year the number was twelve months, maybe six. This April the federal government's own AI testing center called it roughly eight months, and Stanford's AI Index, reading the leaderboards this spring, found the gap between the top American and Chinese models had shrunk to 2.7 percent--no longer a lead so much as a rounding error with good publicists. Yesterday the number arrived at approximately zero, carrying a price tag 40 percent lower than ours and a shipping date for the free copy.
Eighteen, twelve, eight, two-point-seven, zero: a countdown every one of these executives could read the whole time, while they assured Congress and their investors and the rest of us that the moat was real.
**We had mistaken being early for being ahead.**

Beijing just caught us--and is about to give the frontier away for free. | | and | Jul 20| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- by Lawrence Winnerman, Blue Amp Media COO Once you 've finished this, read the companion piece, . On Thursday, July 16th, a company most Americans have never heard of released an artificial intelligence model that caught the American frontier lab models, and it released it from Beijing. The company is called Moonshot AI. The model is Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, the largest model ever slated for open release, and within hours of its debut it stood in first place on Arena's Frontend Code leaderboard, ahead of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, the two most capable systems the American labs have ever shipped--first, in fact, in six of the seven coding categories. On Arena's broader text rankings it finished ahead of Claude Opus 4.8, Anthropic's flagship until five weeks ago, while costing 40 percent less to run. And on Monday, July 27th, Moonshot says, it will give the whole thing away: the weights, the architecture, everything, free to download and free to run in any data center on earth. The weights are the model itself, the billions of numbers in which everything it learned is stored; whoever holds them holds the machine. Moonshot --and, by extension, China, just beat us at AI and is giving the model away. For FREE. Axios said it plainly Friday morning: "China just erased America's AI lead." Eighty years to build, and all it took was one random Thursday to lose. | | ---|---|--- Beijing, China The computer is an American invention. The theory owes a debt to a British mathematician, Turing, who his own government hounded to death, but the machines--the actual, humming, room-filling, world-changing machines--were built here in the United States. In February 1946, in a room at the University of Pennsylvania, engineers threw the switches on ENIAC, thirty tons of vacuum tubes and hand-soldered wire that could do in thirty seconds what a human being with a desk calculator needed twenty hours to finish. The transistor came out of Bell Labs in New Jersey the following year; the integrated circuit out of Texas and California a decade after that; the microprocessor out of Santa Clara in 1971. The supercomputer was substantially the work of one stubborn man in Chippewa Falls, Wisconsin--Seymour Cray, who treated speed as a calling. The internet began as ARPANET, a Pentagon research project that spoke its first halting word between UCLA and the Stanford Research Institute in the autumn of 1969. And the transformer architecture that makes every modern AI model possible--Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and yes, Kimi K3--was published in 2017 by eight researchers at Google, in a paper the company let out the door for free. | | ---|---|--- ENIAC Every layer of this revolution was laid down on American ground, much of it with public money, much of it by people who came here from somewhere else because here was where you came to build. The record reads like myth and is footnoted like history. Computing is the American inheritance the way navigation belonged to Portugal and steel belonged to Sheffield, except bigger, because computing became the substrate everything else now runs on--including steel manufacturing and navigation. I am not a neutral witness to any of this. I spent twenty-five years inside the American tech industry, managing programs at the largest scale it had to offer, and I believed--actually believed, the way you believe things at two in the morning in a war room when the release finally goes green--that we were building the future for everyone. Then the industry decided that people my age were a cost center, the first wave of this technology arrived to absorb our work, and I got to experience the American way of implementing AI from the receiving end. I know what these companies are from the inside, which is why you should believe me when I tell you: this was the home game, the one field we were supposed to lose last, or never at all. In 2023, the men running America's AI industry told us China was eighteen months behind, and eighteen months, at frontier speed, was forever. By last year the number was twelve months, maybe six. This April the federal government's own AI testing center called it roughly eight months, and Stanford's AI Index, reading the leaderboards this spring, found the gap between the top American and Chinese models had shrunk to 2.7 percent--no longer a lead so much as a rounding error with good publicists. Yesterday the number arrived at approximately zero, carrying a price tag 40 percent lower than ours and a shipping date for the free copy. Eighteen, twelve, eight, two-point-seven, zero: a countdown every one of these executives could read the whole time, while they assured Congress and their investors and the rest of us that the moat was real. We had mistaken being early for being ahead. The rest of this essay names names: who sold the American century, why they sold it, and what taking it back actually looks like. Dear Friend,

C.S. Lewis is one of my favorite authors, full stop.

His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible. Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.

Why are Lewis's words so powerful?

It's because he was a master at addressing life's most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.

Lewis's signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

To help you learn more about Lewis's works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course, "**C.S. Lewis on Christianity** ," which you can now own on DVD absolutely free.

**Claim your FREE DVD set of "C.S. Lewis on Christianity" using this secure link:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0U1r3DAQBuBfI99s5JH8dfAhwVkoJC39gByFrJm1B2TJWPKG_PuyZQs99zozzAPv-_5m3ix7DstXu9HIKRmMaJCTizc68koz2TN_2oD5OPNqQEJbyq4EaazLfCOjbYFjA3V_7Qsa667XjR7apivWsZ1nqQhVB3oArUn13dxAq5paQj8DFTze_8kOZA21rlXlLPXDjAr10M2EVmh57mgzVRwSIyUX475Hz5ldquKxFH5cc96TUE8CLgIuHK6xWtn7hNZTRXgKuFwPotKl0tMHp9KtB6fMNnD-LPGGQl2SE2qSEkA9SSnr13qYvk3Ty08B7Zk3k-J5OBJq2o-YdnKZw_JYbYR8bkJNtFn2j6Gz2255CUJNLpk_qvlXNXf1cRpDppCFmp6_PL--mO9d-f7rR_k3l-IYcf9g7zm1ndByuSuVi1uR_7et2wi_AwAA__9k-qcG)

In this course, you will study Lewis's profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* Good and evil
* Conversion and faith
* Prayer and the Bible
* Suffering and death
* Heaven and Hell

The instructor, Michael Ward, is a distinguished visiting professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He wrote _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis 's The Abolition of Man_. He even spent three years living in Lewis's Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!

You'll find this course especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis's beautiful writings about faith. You'll even trace Lewis's own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for you to grow in your knowledge and understanding of Christianity.

[So please join us in studying Christianity with C.S. Lewis and Michael Ward with this beautiful free DVD set.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0U1r3DAQBuBfI99s5JH8dfAhwVkoJC39gByFrJm1B2TJWPKG_PuyZQs99zozzAPv-_5m3ix7DstXu9HIKRmMaJCTizc68koz2TN_2oD5OPNqQEJbyq4EaazLfCOjbYFjA3V_7Qsa667XjR7apivWsZ1nqQhVB3oArUn13dxAq5paQj8DFTze_8kOZA21rlXlLPXDjAr10M2EVmh57mgzVRwSIyUX475Hz5ldquKxFH5cc96TUE8CLgIuHK6xWtn7hNZTRXgKuFwPotKl0tMHp9KtB6fMNnD-LPGGQl2SE2qSEkA9SSnr13qYvk3Ty08B7Zk3k-J5OBJq2o-YdnKZw_JYbYR8bkJNtFn2j6Gz2255CUJNLpk_qvlXNXf1cRpDppCFmp6_PL--mO9d-f7rR_k3l-IYcf9g7zm1ndByuSuVi1uR_7et2wi_AwAA__9k-qcG)

Warm regards,

Bill Gray '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

body:
Peter,

The countdown to Election Day is getting shorter, and our campaign is entering one of the most important phases yet:

**Early voting begins across Missouri TOMORROW and runs through August 3, giving voters the chance to cast their ballots before Election Day on August 4.**

That means every day between now and then is an opportunity to reach another voter, answer another question, and make sure St. Louisans have the information they need to cast their ballot.

We're already hard at work preparing for this final stretch. That looks like: organizing volunteers, talking with voters across the district, and building the strongest Get Out the Vote operation we can, while we still can. But none of that happens without you, Peter.

Lead Story · The Iran War
THREE U.S. TROOPS KILLED AS THE IRAN WAR GRINDS INTO A NINTH NIGHT OF STRIKES
What's Happening
* U.S. Central Command said American forces hit Iran for a **ninth consecutive night** into Monday, striking command centers, air defenses, coastal surveillance, missile and drone sites, and communications networks around the Strait of Hormuz.
* The Pentagon confirmed **three U.S. service members have been killed** — two in an Iranian missile-and-drone attack on a base in Jordan on Friday, and one in northern Iraq on Saturday during a controlled detonation of a downed Iranian drone — bringing U.S. war deaths to **17** since February.
* President Trump vowed to "swiftly punish" Iran and said Tehran has been "very badly damaged."

The Situation
* Iran's health ministry claimed **50 killed and 517 wounded** in the latest U.S. strikes — figures we cannot independently verify.
* Tehran signaled some **openness to talks** , with its foreign ministry saying it had received proposals from mediators — a hint that helped ease oil prices off their highs.
* More than **50,000 U.S. personnel** are deployed across the Middle East, and Gulf hosts Kuwait and Bahrain have absorbed drone and missile damage.

The Perspective
These deaths are the sober cost of a real war, and they deserve more than a talking point: Americans are dying to keep the world's most important oil passage open after Iran tore up the ceasefire. Strength is warranted — but so is a clear objective. "Very badly damaged" is not the same as a defined end state, and nine nights in, the country deserves to hear what victory looks like and when the troops come home.

The Economy
GAS TOPS $4 A GALLON AGAIN AS THE WAR SQUEEZES THE STRAIT — AND YOUR WALLET
What's Happening
* The national average for regular gas climbed back **above $4 a gallon on Monday** — the first time since mid-June — as the fighting choked oil flows through Hormuz.
* Brent crude briefly touched **$90 a barrel** before easing back toward $88 after Iran hinted at dialogue.
* Diesel — which moves trucks and farm equipment — rose to about **$5.10 a gallon**.

The Situation
* Gas is up more than a dollar since the war began; in California, Hawaii, and Washington, averages are at or near **$5**.
* A Brown University analysis estimates the war has already cost Americans more than **$35 billion** in higher fuel costs.
* The IRS took the rare step of raising its mileage deduction midyear, to 76 cents, to reflect the surge.

The Perspective
Whatever one thinks of the war, the bill is landing at the pump — and for working families and small businesses, a dollar-plus jump is real money. A conflict fought partly to keep oil flowing is, for now, doing the opposite at home. Reopening the strait isn't just strategy; it's kitchen-table economics.

Election Integrity
TRUMP'S PRIMETIME ELECTION FILES LAND AS THE SAVE ACT STAYS STUCK
What's Happening
* Last Thursday's primetime address — in which Trump declassified files alleging "shocking vulnerabilities" and Chinese interference — is still reverberating, with the documents posted on the White House site.
* He renewed his push for the **SAVE Act** (proof of citizenship to register, ID to vote), and the RNC chairman echoed the call.
* The bill remains **stalled in the Senate**.

The Situation
* NPR notes intelligence reviews under both the Trump and Biden administrations found no evidence a foreign government altered votes, and that in-person fraud is rare.
* Critics call the rollout long on claims and short on new proof; supporters say the transparency is overdue.
* With the war dominating Washington, floor time for the bill is scarce.

The Perspective
Proof-of-citizenship and voter ID enjoy broad public support and are worth passing. But a primetime spectacle raises the bar: the declassified specifics have to hold up, or the effort hands critics an easy target. The stronger play is legislation that sticks — not relitigating 2020.

War Funding
TROOP DEATHS PUT TRUMP'S $87.6 BILLION WAR REQUEST BEFORE A RAZOR-THIN SENATE
What's Happening
* The American casualties sharpen the stakes on Trump's **$87.6 billion request** to fund the war with Iran, now before a Senate with almost no margin for error.
* Republicans hold a nominal **53–47** edge after Sen. Lindsey Graham's sister was appointed to his seat, but Sen. Mitch McConnell, 84, remains sidelined, recovering from a June fall and pneumonia.
* Majority Leader **John Thune** is trying to move war funding and the stalled SAVE Act with barely a vote to spare.

The Situation
* Graham, the former Budget chairman and a leading defense hawk, died this month; his absence removes a key coalition-builder on national security.
* Republicans have only about **seven weeks** of scheduled session before the November midterms.
* Every holdout now carries outsized leverage over what moves.

The Perspective
War funding shouldn't be a partisan football when troops are in the field — but a one-vote margin makes even must-pass bills fragile. Thune's challenge is arithmetic: hold the conference together, or watch the president's most urgent request stall at the worst possible moment.

⚡ The Bottom Line
The war with Iran has turned deadly for Americans: three service members killed and a ninth straight night of U.S. strikes, even as Tehran hints at talks and oil pushes gas back over four dollars a gallon at home. In Washington, the casualties raise the stakes on Trump's $87.6 billion war request before a razor-thin Senate, while his election-integrity push still waits for a floor vote. **A nation grieving fallen troops, paying more at the pump, and watching a hair's-breadth Senate decide what gets funded. That's just the truth.**

The Pentagon confirmed three U.S. service members have been killed — two in an Iranian missile-and-drone attack on a base in Jordan on Friday, and one in northern Iraq on Saturday during a controlled detonation of a downed Iranian drone — bringing U.S. war deaths to 17 since February. President Trump vowed to "swiftly punish" Iran and said Tehran has been "very badly damaged." The Situation Iran's health ministry claimed 50 killed and 517 wounded in the latest U.S. strikes — figures we cannot independently verify. Tehran signaled some openness to talks , with its foreign ministry saying it had received proposals from mediators — a hint that helped ease oil prices off their highs. More than 50,000 U.S. personnel are deployed across the Middle East, and Gulf hosts Kuwait and Bahrain have absorbed drone and missile damage. The Perspective These deaths are the sober cost of a real war, and they deserve more than a talking point: Americans are dying to keep the world's most important oil passage open after Iran tore up the ceasefire. Strength is warranted — but so is a clear objective. "Very badly damaged" is not the same as a defined end state, and nine nights in, the country deserves to hear what victory looks like and when the troops come home. The Economy GAS TOPS $4 A GALLON AGAIN AS THE WAR SQUEEZES THE STRAIT — AND YOUR WALLET What's Happening The national average for regular gas climbed back above $4 a gallon on Monday — the first time since mid-June — as the fighting choked oil flows through Hormuz. Brent crude briefly touched $90 a barrel before easing back toward $88 after Iran hinted at dialogue. Diesel — which moves trucks and farm equipment — rose to about $5.10 a gallon. The Situation Gas is up more than a dollar since the war began; in California, Hawaii, and Washington, averages are at or near $5. A Brown University analysis estimates the war has already cost Americans more than $35 billion in higher fuel costs. The IRS took the rare step of raising its mileage deduction midyear, to 76 cents, to reflect the surge. The Perspective Whatever one thinks of the war, the bill is landing at the pump — and for working families and small businesses, a dollar-plus jump is real money. A conflict fought partly to keep oil flowing is, for now, doing the opposite at home. Reopening the strait isn't just strategy; it's kitchen-table economics. He renewed his push for the SAVE Act (proof of citizenship to register, ID to vote), and the RNC chairman echoed the call. The bill remains stalled in the Senate. The Situation NPR notes intelligence reviews under both the Trump and Biden administrations found no evidence a foreign government altered votes, and that in-person fraud is rare. Critics call the rollout long on claims and short on new proof; supporters say the transparency is overdue. With the war dominating Washington, floor time for the bill is scarce. The Perspective Proof-of-citizenship and voter ID enjoy broad public support and are worth passing. But a primetime spectacle raises the bar: the declassified specifics have to hold up, or the effort hands critics an easy target. The stronger play is legislation that sticks — not relitigating 2020. Republicans hold a nominal 53–47 edge after Sen. Lindsey Graham's sister was appointed to his seat, but Sen. Mitch McConnell, 84, remains sidelined, recovering from a June fall and pneumonia. Majority Leader John Thune is trying to move war funding and the stalled SAVE Act with barely a vote to spare. The Situation Graham, the former Budget chairman and a leading defense hawk, died this month; his absence removes a key coalition-builder on national security. Republicans have only about seven weeks of scheduled session before the November midterms. Every holdout now carries outsized leverage over what moves. Thune's challenge is arithmetic: hold the conference together, or watch the president's most urgent request stall at the worst possible moment. ⚡ The Bottom Line The war with Iran has turned deadly for Americans: three service members killed and a ninth straight night of U.S. strikes, even as Tehran hints at talks and oil pushes gas back over four dollars a gallon at home. In Washington, the casualties raise the stakes on Trump's $87.6 billion war request before a razor-thin Senate, while his election-integrity push still waits for a floor vote. We need volunteers for the following roles:
* Communications Director
* Social Media Manager

name: Andrew Hodge
subject: Help Us Elect Tessa Lynn Hodge – Leaders & Volunteers Needed
body:
Hello,

I hope you're doing well. You are receiving this email because at some
point you've connected with Tessa's campaign, attended one of our community
events, participated in one of NotStepping Back's demonstrations, or
expressed an interest in getting involved. Some of these email lists go
back quite a while, so if your circumstances have changed, I completely
understand. However, if you're still looking for a way to make a
difference, I'd love to invite you to join our team.

As we continue building our grassroots campaign, we're looking for *both
department leaders and team members*. Whether you're interested in helping
lead a team or volunteering a few hours each week, there is a place for you.
Field Team

Our Field Team is the backbone of our voter outreach efforts. We're looking
for both *Field Team Leaders* and *Field Team Members* to help:

-

Organize and lead neighborhood literature drops.
-

Distribute campaign literature to voters' homes.
-

Identify friends, neighbors, businesses, or community members who may be
interested in hosting a *Meet the Candidate* event or fundraiser.
-

Recruit and coordinate additional volunteers.
-

Assist with community outreach and campaign events throughout the
district.

Finance Team

A successful grassroots campaign depends on strong fundraising support.
We're seeking *Finance Team Leaders* and *Finance Team Members* to assist
with:

-

Researching prospective donors using campaign-approved resources.
-

Gathering and organizing donor contact information.
-

Assisting Tessa during call time, when she personally reaches out to
supporters and potential donors.
-

Joining Zoom sessions during call time to take notes, manage donor
information, and help keep the program running smoothly.
-

Coordinating follow-up tasks after donor calls.

Social Media Team

Our Social Media Team helps share Tessa's vision with voters across the
district. We're looking for volunteers interested in:

-

Writing and editing content.
-

Creating social media posts.
-

Researching information, policies, and local issues.
-

Graphic design.
-

Video editing and production.
-

Photography and videography.
-

Developing creative campaign messaging.

Whether you're an experienced professional or simply want to learn and
contribute, your time and talents can make a meaningful difference.

Every conversation, every flyer delivered, every donor contacted, and every
hour volunteered strengthens this campaign. Grassroots campaigns are
powered by people, and we'd be honored to have you as part of our team.

If you're interested, simply reply to this email and let me know:

-

Which department interests you or anyway you can help.
-

Whether you'd like to serve in a *leadership role* or as a *team member*.
-

Any skills or experience you'd like to bring to the campaign.

Thank you for your continued support. Together, we can build the campaign
our district deserves and elect Tessa Lynn Hodge to Congress.

Sincerely,

Andrew Hodge

*Andrew Hodge*[image: transparent_vintage_border_image.png]

Founder- NotStepping Back

Senior Campaign Advisor

Tessa Lynn Hodge for Congress

Andrew@TessaForCA.com
(760) 235-0558

There was a guy named Plutarch around 50 A.D. -- two thousand years ago -- who warned the Athenians that the imbalance between the rich and the poor is the oldest and most fatal ailments of all republics.
Fast forward to today...
We've minted the first trillionaire and more than two dozen states still have a minimum wage of $7.25 an hour. The wealthy in this country have never had it so good, while millions of Americans are struggling to get by.

name: Dan Osborn
subject: The Senate is a Country Club
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY OSBORN FOR SENATE
body:
If I win in November, I will be the least wealthy member of the U.S. Senate.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001MYVvs0z561zh38HpyScrRTDRG94jI1ELINyZNgNPX9aSG49cZHkCLN8TzIOkpwRylVuiy4P2IZ2VM5tmZxnM7Y-uUDYzNR49AKSlLl5WisNXw1OcFHOxwrMgZLFoYZEZjPSmRIgl1PmKgpzm20LnE02xS-O8i07-lDDLg6kFcClhyIJhhU_hdMdy117J7DHRI-AIitzZ8U8azotVdSDj_8OzsV8ouHM2V3Xl4SiDcaQ=&c=OmhoIALpf6CwnNA0V13jSERhdsXGnGu14n5E5hgLgOMrESGY0aWjgg==&ch=BKuY_l2yd7lV7Ao3qqBj-M8TEzWOCOUnnS1_EYdM_uxE4OULrkfstg==)
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001MYVvs0z561zh38HpyScrRTDRG94jI1ELINyZNgNPX9aSG49cZHkCLN8TzIOkpwRylVuiy4P2IZ2VM5tmZxnM7Y-uUDYzNR49AKSlLl5WisNXw1OcFHOxwrMgZLFoYZEZjPSmRIgl1PmKgpzm20LnE02xS-O8i07-lDDLg6kFcClhyIJhhU_hdMdy117J7DHRI-AIitzZ8U8azotVdSDj_8OzsV8ouHM2miDBSO4WXfY=&c=OmhoIALpf6CwnNA0V13jSERhdsXGnGu14n5E5hgLgOMrESGY0aWjgg==&ch=BKuY_l2yd7lV7Ao3qqBj-M8TEzWOCOUnnS1_EYdM_uxE4OULrkfstg==)
---
Peter,
The U.S. Senate is a country club. It's full of billionaires, former business execs, lawyers with Ivy League degrees, and trust fund kids born with so many silver spoons in their mouths that they have no idea the reality for working-class people like me.
If I defeat my opponent, the literal billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts, I will be the least wealthy member of the U.S. Senate. I don't come from money, and I'm not rich. I'm a steamfitter and mechanic who's worked 50- and 60-hour workweeks my whole life to give my kids a better life.
I will be the only senator without a college degree. After my wife and I found out we were expecting a baby, I had to drop out and kill my dream of hanging a diploma on the wall because my family needed health insurance, diapers, and food on the table.
I will be the only senator who is a blue-collar, card-carrying union member. When Kellogg's tried to cut our benefits and workers' pay, we risked it all, went on strike, and walked the picket line for 11 weeks through the bitter cold Nebraska winter. We won and saved hundreds of good-paying jobs - before I was fired for being the union president who led the strike.
There is no one who represents working-class people like me in the U.S. Senate. But in 2024, ours was one of the closest Senate races in the country. And the latest poll for 2026 shows me LEADING Republican Pete Ricketts in 2026 - 47% to 46%.
I've taken on a big corporation before and won, and now I'm going to defeat a literal billionaire - my opponent Republican Pete Ricketts - and win this Senate seat. But I need your help to do it.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | Jacob Davis's Market Brief (ads) | • | Awesomely ---|--- • | Safe Money Report • | Weiss Ratings | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. My story starts in Great Falls.

Friend,

My name is Kurt Alme, and I want to introduce myself.

I was born in Great Falls in 1966. My dad taught high school math. My mom taught elementary school. We didn't have a lot, but we had everything that mattered: hard work, faith, and a deep sense of neighborliness.
[](http://links.m.rightnationalerts.com/s/c/HHfBYibKIIl6SHMPJdnEzU3V36025sG3L68ra6DJE66bwcX9ionNeCPFgAAmD5ZVQVqNPwCs1IA1jXVqgqSimTJwZCo-kQQ1FBHEkIwF22r8q-tjCcCcwAZiCJ6acgnVA6SAkybBHn79YvQrJYcNhlgOiOFs2pZHpKVmV4T2xJYkZUdOM1QtCWqALHpE0xDbucBEFlrKIYau8ZsWyL-Y2Tz9sOX5e4d8ycGO7EvjKe6S2G2FpgrkwHKWOdP37iHp7wU4C8o40tNXPhMLM78ilhmPdzME4YSdefyTiVG-S4R5efVTYi4INKZLFCbflosEOo9faJ0Eh1UqDAbxJrTkIWsN2cLaAWd-N4SFD6R4OASgspO-6R_wY-IwQktMHTw4qSBQ6RS6RX2bDiI9SQU3DLlygAXQ3MwUtWzQOfn5RbbqFkyN5YfEgqy6TmwnZ9BmpSTOUHlY99oUZl8eVUwbO9v5_DoBrRwtwPdd-UC-GrhrlNyV35mgSZcNdC9UijzMwsDlCGILe9uVf641V4p9mwhikrDodk1GQpbBsHjyfqz7w3VIgbNe0tvH0p4aFhOhYAFpOah5YammW-t_LVajgZhe7HLdE8zPfq_J2k03Hpqe0dWM0I7uyYCqAQuZB4vYOLmUQtif-KVE7oLyzXiXTRvbtGdFv0D83ggFsBGeIu8Deyr62bJ4CnwK5IXrekJmJuP6rZxrl8iy2F4UCxwvvX6JekdSao7nx913lvosdlr6QAhq7cUhOZ7Nt_OUovWIscLXG-F6Y9zONIWjwIu54pRWHrU6VUBN-ydVoAmnwoJT2iFcD-6oBQcYfTtD6tA_2kLsiIJGZ3IDZvldKYAhjo6ofHs4snydPXpjmFfnsd1r2g5Dxwfn3XV0i8H4phMW-aCkZqr6Jxgy-IUk00Bg5ESi4GzdRZT5J5YyxBHncwotFryfl5y1X7LYrTw1aYROHLnAbgLKIFf0ZBNisZRji8ja2ONoL9HAvDs5XugP1dswJObYmcpVd1pbp4Iw5siTpWbU0-iKTZ136r3YBiL3LhELHA/qujHd0dFvLd0Xzbs00y7nAM3A3n18KYT/22)
As my dad's career moved, so did we. Dillon. Victor. Helena. Miles City. I went to school in small towns, played football on Friday nights, and grew up surrounded by the kind of Montanans who built this place with their hands and their character.

I never forgot where I came from.

After high school, I went to college in Colorado and then to Harvard Law School - graduating with my conservative values intact and stronger than ever. Once I had my degree in hand, I came straight back home. Montana was always where I was meant to be.

I built a legal career here. Raised my family here with my wife Sandra, who I have been married to for 31 years. And I got deeply involved in the community here.

As Director of the Montana Department of Revenue, I helped spearhead the largest income tax rate cut in our history and put money back in Montanans' pockets. As U.S. Attorney, nominated by President Trump and confirmed by the Senate, I focused on prosecuting violent criminals, drug traffickers, and cartels that were poisoning our communities. Most recently, our office prosecuted more defendants than in any year over the past two decades.

Now I'm running for United States Senate.
[](http://links.m.rightnationalerts.com/s/c/d34FNlxxqQDqiLHOhGvZHn2Ci6cu8xsLd-es7SuQV34THM8kh4N380zXHvG8bIljnuZG4R63us4GCwMXOIGDF8dsyfSxNNYGlXAupqqvabI3btX5xrQfLweWFFmj-wG_cWKA08ijTlBLrZbiqxVCvL6l5uGn8PXkPNsLnGTkx0X93NAqZbM80RrA5mPpSV-NZ8NAIXcV74FaLy6q5YY8qg3NMhq14hOZqPvJhfakNTyMj4P8T23RaXGN8aDhymHzOU8m6v5VzmUhkpMR7jrSuo0aUwiJPE8s8kjkWQEBnlutgyVosmn1N9NTCV8dGM9WPSkRc12rmm5YaLz6CMvl2RhSp8LTKhtNVs1zDXjnKJCXDPsKtJBAPjyIcCUePx1nLKDc68XNC69fhnGitJe7NgAZ10m1xLh-FE6JUTZb9iByaqNfh6NYtr44X5FXV5QOz-vKkLs29A84y6rKNe4JXixpxNmEgG1cSF8eW7jKKFoe2lKn-bmZ-2HQ_iNQoRnbqFYf2hFDkQh_PJDgrGFSvZKQLDOJwfcJVl0ptZuMKtdlPhdZZzEs_xj1hYuL9d8aHxqluzLV4DGXpjBTFTydWzRGjFoRoom8n4teq8ocdQxuX_QRlOrs3C-oYYxSCPP1p_NHULJs2ysXdqBAukr_VfSc5zrTjk5xnc-VnteRyfEageNK-dkhOi-PI9pBHo83unf_f5lvMHOxxbnkm1VG9wxZY0kMh9CGdryWk5IPN81DbI5ZUGwn7JbBxgGz-qN9b5Xy8aE6WVdIoTw49e8CcR6N4wCOpVRAWMoVwUbQgMk7NZWdJ2KfcLZezT-BBM2Rzo0-oU5t3vtwyvYfw7wmuPseQwCgP9fxEou-ej4J7Hv_IfzjTfD_I9vcKZxLGGwUBLdFmVTzEfW9xF_OUfQ2q-J5GFlIQpv7NzIC3Z07jWyrf_NOcVLutdGstdslcb8-PfOQRymLoqjk38Fru_2znAxhgkDbF1ADSIgLM2zztb1xlI2iTLOGiv7u_m9TI3LOpzz6eK77eQvAOWThZsAVLjHKYA/IAc7tUYTKu5TOmmI3EFbOBwugK0vilGC/22)
Not because it's easy and not because I was looking for the next thing, but because I believe Montana needs a senator who has actually lived here, worked here, and fought for the people here.

I would be honored to earn your support. **[Please consider chipping in a donation of any amount to help me fund my campaign and win this race. NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani gave a halting answer when **[pressed by the New York Times to define who qualifies as"working class"](https://substack.com/redirect/6daf4b8b-7123-4c38-9523-2ecf8a714432?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**, the constituency he claims to champion. "I haven't sat at home and asked myself where it starts and stops. Oftentimes we're asked how we divide this country. I think there's only one majority in this country -- it's the working class," Mamdani answered.
