I need to tell you something I don't talk about enough.
Outside of my office, a group of extremists gathered and screamed what translates to "Death to Krishnamoorthi" at the top of their lungs.
A crowd of people, in America, calling for my death.
I'm an immigrant. The son of people who came to this country with nothing because they believed it was a place where you could live freely, speak freely, and serve your community without fearing for your life. A place where disagreement didn't end in threats of violence.
Sadly, this is nothing new. I have faced this before.
A sitting Republican elected official also publicly tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media to report me as a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name" and called for the mass deportation of Indians. I have been mocked, threatened, and told in a hundred different ways that someone like me doesn't belong in American public life.
And every single time, I have made the same choice.
Keep going.
Because the moment I stop — the moment I let the hatred win — is the moment I break faith with every family that came to this country believing it was worth fighting for. Including my own.
This is the America we are living in right now. Extremists feel emboldened to threaten, intimidate, and silence the people who are trying to do the work. Hatred has been given permission to operate in the open. The machinery of government is being used to make certain communities feel like they don't belong.
Equal Opportunity Now exists because we need leaders who have faced this kind of hatred and didn't flinch. Who know what it costs to keep going and choose to keep going anyway. Who will stand up — not just for themselves, but for every family that is being targeted, threatened, and told they don't belong.
Those leaders are out there. And they need our support right now.

Peter,

Education opened doors that changed the course of Christina's life. It gave her opportunities and helped her build the future she dreamed of. It's why she's so passionate about making sure every child has the same chance to get ahead.

You can't solve differential equations if you never learned your numbers in kindergarten. You can't become a great writer if you never learned to read. Every lesson and every school year lays the foundation for what comes next. **She believes every child deserves a well-funded public school that will help them succeed at all levels, whether they live in the heart of a city or in one of Iowa's rural communities.**

Unfortunately, that's not the direction Mariannette Miller-Meeks has chosen. She supported Iowa's private school voucher program, then backed a national voucher plan that's roughly ten times larger, diverting even more taxpayer dollars away from public schools. She's attacked teachers during congressional hearings and voted for an extreme budget that would eliminate more than 100,000 teaching jobs across the country. This is unacceptable.

He just invited a dozen friends over to his house to pray. But that was enough for the City of University Heights, Ohio, to send him a cease-and-desist letter, urge neighbors to spy on him, deny him tax abatements, and periodically stop collecting his trash. All because an Orthodox Jewish man--whose faith prevents him from driving to synagogue on the Sabbath--gathered with friends to pray in his own home. Lower federal courts dismissed his case, ruling Daniel had to complete a permit process he never should have faced in the first place. Even worse: Daniel learned that if he had obtained the permit, his home would have been designated a house of worship, and his family would no longer be allowed to live there. But the United States Supreme Court just agreed to hear _Grand v. City of University Heights_ --and ADF is on it. What's at stake goes far beyond one man's home. Thirty-one percent of Evangelical Christians meet in home small groups. Orthodox Jewish minyans like Daniel's, house church gatherings, and home Bible studies all depend on the very freedom Daniel is fighting to exercise. If the city prevails, local governments across the country will have a blueprint: label any home religious gathering a zoning violation, bury the resident in red tape, and then argue that federal courts can't step in. That's a free-exercise emergency. ADF attorneys--alongside co-counsel Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe--are now preparing to argue before the highest court in the land that Americans cannot be locked out of federal courts simply because officials manufactured a bureaucratic maze around their constitutional rights. **The Founders were clear: You don 't need a government permit to pray with friends in your own home.** Your ongoing generosity is what helps put ADF in front of the Supreme Court--please make a gift today to keep cases like Daniel's moving forward. Cancer screenings. Diabetes prevention. HIV prevention.
These aren't partisan issues. They're basic healthcare.
And yet, for the fourth time, RFK’s Department of Health and Human Services has blocked a meeting of the independent panel that reviews the science behind preventive care in America.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?]
The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force exists for one reason: to carefully evaluate the evidence and recommend which preventive services help save lives.
Those recommendations don't just guide doctors — they also determine what health insurance plans must cover for millions of Americans.
Their work isn't supposed to be political. But under RFK Jr., the panel hasn't met in person in well over a year.
As a microbiologist, I find this deeply troubling.
Science doesn't stop because it's politically inconvenient. Cancer, diabetes, and disease don’t wait. And every day that independent experts are prevented from doing their jobs is another day Americans are denied the benefit of evidence-based public health.
I've spent my career teaching students to ask questions, follow the evidence, and let the facts lead us where they lead.
That's exactly the opposite of what we're seeing in Washington. Instead of letting scientists do their work, this administration keeps sidelining them.
That's why I'm running for Congress. We need leaders who understand that science isn't a partisan issue. Public health isn't a partisan issue. The health of our families shouldn't depend on who's in power. If you're ready to send a scientist to Congress who will fight for evidence-based policymaking, I'd be grateful for your support today. Those recommendations don't just guide doctors — they also determine what health insurance plans must cover for millions of Americans. Their work isn't supposed to be political. But under RFK Jr., the panel hasn't met in person in well over a year. As a microbiologist, I find this deeply troubling. Science doesn't stop because it's politically inconvenient. Cancer, diabetes, and disease don’t wait. And every day that independent experts are prevented from doing their jobs is another day Americans are denied the benefit of evidence-based public health. I've spent my career teaching students to ask questions, follow the evidence, and let the facts lead us where they lead. That's exactly the opposite of what we're seeing in Washington. Instead of letting scientists do their work, this administration keeps sidelining them. That's why I'm running for Congress. We need leaders who understand that science isn't a partisan issue. Public health isn't a partisan issue. The health of our families shouldn't depend on who's in power. If you're ready to send a scientist to Congress who will fight for evidence-based policymaking, I'd be grateful for your support today. | | I'm grateful to Governor McMaster for his steady leadership in this difficult moment, and for entrusting Lindsey's sister, Darline Graham Nordone, to carry on her brother's service in the United States Senate. There is no more fitting tribute to Lindsey's remarkable life and his unwavering love for South Carolina than to have Darline finish his term.
But the fight for our state is far from over. Too many South Carolina families are struggling to make ends meet. High gas prices and soaring grocery costs are hurting hardworking people every single day. We need a conservative fighter in the United States Senate who actually delivers results and will stand with President Trump to get our country back on track.
Make no mistake: socialist Democrats want to put this Senate seat in play. They've recruited candidates like Annie Andrews, who would bring the same woke, far-left agenda to South Carolina that has hurt families all across America. Our state deserves a Senator who will stand with President Trump, not stand in his way.

| | Of the many things Lindsey Graham believed in, standing with President Trump and advancing the Republican agenda were among his defining principles. There is no replacing him, but I believe the best way to honor his legacy is to fight alongside the President for his America First agenda just as steadfastly as he did: securing our border, restoring fiscal responsibility, lowering costs for families, defending our God-given constitutional freedoms, and always putting South Carolina first.
The risk to President Trump's agenda is real. We must save the Senate. There's too much at stake to take a chance, so I'm answering the call, and with the special primary on Tuesday, August 11, I'd be honored to have you with me.
Thank you and God bless you,

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

clean_body: There's too much at stake to take a chance | | | | = | | Patriot, Last week, we lost a legendary leader, and I lost a good friend. This week, we face what comes next. I've been overwhelmed by the kind words and encouragement asking me to step up, and today I'm announcing my candidacy for the United States Senate. | | | = | | I'm grateful to Governor McMaster for his steady leadership in this difficult moment, and for entrusting Lindsey's sister, Darline Graham Nordone, to carry on her brother's service in the United States Senate. There is no more fitting tribute to Lindsey's remarkable life and his unwavering love for South Carolina than to have Darline finish his term. But the fight for our state is far from over. Too many South Carolina families are struggling to make ends meet. High gas prices and soaring grocery costs are hurting hardworking people every single day. We need a conservative fighter in the United States Senate who actually delivers results and will stand with President Trump to get our country back on track. Make no mistake: socialist Democrats want to put this Senate seat in play. They've recruited candidates like Annie Andrews, who would bring the same woke, far-left agenda to South Carolina that has hurt families all across America. Our state deserves a Senator who will stand with President Trump, not stand in his way. | | | = | | Of the many things Lindsey Graham believed in, standing with President Trump and advancing the Republican agenda were among his defining principles. There is no replacing him, but I believe the best way to honor his legacy is to fight alongside the President for his America First agenda just as steadfastly as he did: securing our border, restoring fiscal responsibility, lowering costs for families, defending our God-given constitutional freedoms, and always putting South Carolina first. The risk to President Trump's agenda is real. We must save the Senate. There's too much at stake to take a chance, so I'm answering the call, and with the special primary on Tuesday, August 11, I'd be honored to have you with me. Thank you and God bless you, | | = | | Russell FryRepublican Candidate for U.S. Senate | | | = | | | Meet Russell: Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. I was on MSNBC earlier this week to respond to Donald Trump's primetime address.
I put it plainly: This is old news. Donald Trump lost the election fair and square and he's trying to sew distrust in the 2026 elections AND maybe even interfere in upcoming elections.
That's it. That's the whole thing.
Thursday night, the President of the United States took over primetime television to tell the country — again, six years later — that the 2020 election was rigged. He declassified a stack of documents he says prove "shocking vulnerabilities" in our elections. He floated a new allegations about China.
Twenty-five minutes. Not one piece of evidence that a single vote was changed anywhere.
It's pathetic. The President of The United States still can't say the words "I lost."
But pathetic isn't the problem. Dangerous is the problem.
We've seen this movie. In 2020, Trump told this same lie, and it ended with a mob storming the Capitol. He pardoned nearly every one of them. Now he's laying the same groundwork four months before a midterm his party is on track to lose.
He isn't relitigating 2020. He's writing his excuse for November in advance. And he's telling us, out loud, what he plans to do about it.
One more thing nobody should miss: Trump gave that address in the middle of an unauthorized war. Our military has been striking Iran six nights running. Gas prices are climbing. Analysts are warning about a forever war with no way out. By talking about China and the elections, Trump is trying to distract attention from his unpopular failures at home and abroad.
Moments like these are why I built Equal Opportunity Now. We need leaders who will defend our elections, demand answers on this war, and refuse to let a president run out the clock with a primetime temper tantrum.

The Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Michigan is now a two-way race — and I just officially endorsed Abdul El-Sayed. Here's why: Abdul is THE fighter Michigan needs in the Senate. Michigan families deserve a senator who will fight for them — not special interests running millions in TV ads to buy this seat. Abdul is the only candidate in this race that can build the grassroots movement needed to win in November — and we need to make sure he has all the resources he needs to compete with millions of outside spending. [**The primary is just weeks away on August 4, and this race is close. Will you split a contribution of $28 — or whatever you can — to help give Abdul El-Sayed the resources he needs to compete, win this primary, and keep fighting for working people?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3710?amount=28&t=8&akid=2964%2E4032634%2EMtP9sH)

Abdul is a doctor and card-carrying union member who has spent his career standing up for working people. That's why the United Auto Workers endorsed him — and why a grassroots progressive movement is growing across Michigan to support him. Abdul has never taken a dime of corporate PAC money and he never will. His campaign is powered by people, not billionaires or corporate special interests that have spent decades rigging our economy against working families. His opponent is backed by outside special interests pouring millions into Michigan to stop Abdul. We’ve seen this before, and we know what we need to do to defeat them. The only way to beat big money is with a people-powered movement. That's how we've won before, and it's how we'll win again. [**So I'm asking you directly: Will you split a $28 contribution between this movement and Abdul's campaign to help him win this primary and send a strong progressive fighter to the U.S. Senate?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3710?amount=28&t=14&akid=2964%2E4032634%2EMtP9sH) Let's elect someone who will fight to put more money in people's pockets, get big money out of politics, and finally deliver Medicare for All. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

# Iran and Ceasefire
* **U.S. continues its strikes on Iran over the weekend and into Monday:** The U.S. [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/bc102aa0-7006-44b7-bc8c-b60429da0c45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several waves of strikes on Iran over the weekend; one attack hit a nuclear power plant.
* On Saturday, after its eighth consecutive night of strikes, CENTCOM said that it had successfully targeted "Iranian military coastal surveillance and air defense facilities, maritime capabilities, and missile and drone storage sites." The announcement also claimed successful hits on IRGC forces, though no casualty figures were given.
* The U.S. struck Iran's Darkhovin nuclear power plant on Sunday, according to the country's Atomic Energy Agency. * **Troy Jackson effectively secures Democratic Senate nomination in Maine: Troy Jackson** won [more](https://substack.com/redirect/2f1184c2-c771-4ff1-a2c6-d128673dd925?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than 90% of delegates in county elections held over the weekend to become Maine's replacement Democratic Senate nominee, positioning him to secure the nomination at a July 25 convention in Bangor, Drop Site contributor Nathan Bernard reports.
* Jackson, a former state senator who leveraged the organizing network of previous nominee **Graham Platner** , will face Sen. **Susan Collins** in November after his top rivals, **Shenna Bellows** and **Nirav Shah** , dropped out and endorsed him Sunday.
* **Mamdani says Netanyahu arrest still under discussion ahead of UN visit** : Mayor **Zohran Mamdani** [said](https://substack.com/redirect/598becb0-9079-41d9-aacf-9a8b68da7ef5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an interview with The New York Times this weekend that his administration is weighing whether to arrest **Netanyahu** if he visits New York for the U.N. General Assembly in September, saying he is in "active conversation" with the city's Law Department over his legal authority to do so.
* The Mayor noted Netanyahu's ICC arrest warrant, calling him "a war criminal." Mamdani condemned U.S. policy towards Gaza, saying "It is hard to find a more bankrupt policy approach" than America's conduct towards Gaza and Palestine.
* Mamdani commented on immigration policy, saying he was "willing to work" with the Trump administration when immigrants were convicted of "serious crimes," but said he refused to participate in civil immigration enforcement operations "with a federal government that has said openly it wants to deport a vast majority of people for crimes that we will never even know."
* When asked about a possible presidential run from his New York colleague, Rep. **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** , he said she would "make a good anything."
* **GEO Group employee shoots protester outside Aurora ICE facility** : **Brandon Booth** , a 42-year-old GEO Group employee, was [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/c147966d-41cf-4685-91e5-2f110c198c03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and charged with assault and attempted second-degree murder on Saturday, after police said he shot and wounded a protester Thursday evening outside the Aurora ICE Processing Center in Colorado.
* Aurora police said Booth fired at two women who were involved in a "verbal confrontation" as part of a protest outside the facility. Booth, who was off-duty, reportedly grabbed his personal pistol and fired a shot in their direction.
* **FBI reportedly stepping back from investigating assaults on ICE agents** : The FBI [notified](https://substack.com/redirect/636696c1-3be8-4247-8afc-d86c11f4a13d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) agents in recent days it would stop investigating claims of assaults against Department of Homeland Security agents, a change that would likely shift such cases to ICE's own Homeland Security Investigations division, The New York Times reported on Saturday.
* In addition to the fact that the change would effectively leave ICE with the responsibility of investigating itself, the Times also notes that these investigations were often sources of valuable information to potential civil rights cases against or prosecutions of ICE agents, a more salient concern in the Trump administration's ongoing violent immigration crackdown.
* The Justice Department and DHS issued a joint statement denying any policy change.
* **Chicago U.S. attorney 's office in crisis after immigration prosecution failures**: The U.S. attorney's office in Chicago has [seen](https://substack.com/redirect/ac6fa11f-9a62-446a-9195-8624be14bbef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an exodus of veteran prosecutors and lost 59 of 62 federal assault cases brought against immigrants and protesters during last fall's Operation Midway Blitz, The New York Times reported on Sunday, with only one guilty plea and no convictions.
* More than 100 former federal prosecutors from the office signed a letter criticizing the current U.S. Attorney **Andrew Boutros** , and a judge admonished him this year over his handling of the "Broadview Six" case. "Your sole goal is to do justice," the judge told Boutros in May. She added, "That trust has been broken."
* **Trump order halted federal probe into BAE shipyard harassment claims** : A two-year federal investigation into sexual harassment and pay discrimination against women at a BAE Systems shipyard in Norfolk, Virginia, was abruptly [halted](https://substack.com/redirect/8a1dee90-6fe8-4298-9528-6910677a36de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after **Trump** 's January 2025 executive order shut down most work at the Labor Department's Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs, The New York Times reported on Sunday.
* Investigators, who had documented claims that managers demanded sex acts for overtime and promotions and were nearing a proposed settlement, said the workers never received compensation.
* The office, which has jurisdiction over approximately 20% of the U.S. workforce, has shrunk from about 480 employees to roughly 75. Trump's budget proposal calls for eliminating it entirely.
* **Rep. Summer Lee, national DSA endorse Donovan McKinney in Detroit:** The House Democrat with the most impressive record of choosing primary winners this cycle, **Summer Lee** , is throwing her weight behind state Rep. **Donovan McKinney** , who is challenging AIPAC-backed Rep. **Shri Thanedar** in Michigan. McKinney already had the support of the local Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) chapter, but has now added backing from national. Thanedar, meanwhile, [announced the endorsement ](https://substack.com/redirect/12dbbc80-12d0-4f11-997a-ade865c7a685?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)of the top three House Democrats. The primary is August 4; [McKinney appeared](https://substack.com/redirect/4ae19f77-4927-4b77-b383-b1c6bb4df17e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week on Breaking Points.
* **Elizabeth Warren[ backs Abdul El-Sayed](https://substack.com/redirect/96998ab7-debe-4709-aad4-67f92a33ad3b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Michigan Senate race: **The Massachusetts senator had been backing Mallory McMorrow before she dropped out. That primary is also August 4.
* **Arizona House primary tomorrow is next chance at incumbent upset:** Leftist activist **Kai Newkirk** is challenging Democratic Rep. **Greg Stanton** , a leader of the pro-business New Democrat Coalition, in Arizona's 4th congressional district. Polls show the early vote slanted toward Stanton, but with Newkirk surging and performing well among young voters.

# Other International News
* **Andy Burnham becomes UK prime minister, succeeding Starmer:** Andy Burnham was [appointed](https://substack.com/redirect/1ffe5983-a24c-4079-8d1e-73af5870175c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) British prime minister on Monday, assuming the position without a challenge after Keir Starmer agreed to step down last month following election defeats and scandals.
* He has promised to alleviate England's cost-of-living crisis and save its National Health Service, and in his introductory speech, he said his government would pass "power from the authorities to ordinary people."
* Burnham, who served as mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to 2026 before being elected to Parliament in June, becomes Britain's seventh prime minister in just over a decade.
* **Ansarallah announces maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia:** Yemen's Ansarallah [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/0eae1b3a-24f5-48b2-b9ad-680dfc2a9e86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an immediate maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, saying it was responding to the kingdom's blockade with a "blockade for blockade."
* In a statement, the Yemeni Armed Forces said Saudi Arabia had imposed a land, sea and air blockade on Yemen for nearly 12 years, accusing it of plundering the country's resources and saying the latest escalation began with the strike on Sana'a International Airport. The group warned that any further Saudi escalation would be met with a "comprehensive and decisive" response.
* The announcement follows mass rallies across Yemen and comes after [Ansarallah told Drop Site](https://substack.com/redirect/44ec4abb-e7b9-4b9c-859e-7e67e8cc811c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week it would seek to block Saudi access to the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
* **U.S. to allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium:** The Trump administration has [reached](https://substack.com/redirect/7dbd0799-f484-4747-8fc0-efbd3f271b87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a provisional deal that would allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium, CNN reported on Saturday, though Trump himself has not yet signed the deal.
* The deal, which was negotiated in October 2025, does not require the Kingdom to adopt the IAEA's enhanced safeguards protocol.
* **Sudan updates:**
* Sudan's Army [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/3a85ceaf-97f1-4376-a593-babbae39843f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a renewed push in the North Darfur region, particularly on Rapid Support Forces (RSF) positions near the border with Chad, according to Mada Masr, which reported that at least 300 vehicles had crossed the desert into the area in the preceding week. The buildup follows RSF operations in nearby Um Baru, which have affected upwards of 50 towns and villages and displaced over 4,000 people, according to the outlet.
* An RSF siege on the North Kordofan city of El Obeid [damaged](https://substack.com/redirect/dcbfb16f-0086-42a6-be89-18aff21f9bc1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the city's main water source, reducing the city's water output by 70 percent, Madr Masr reported on Saturday. The city, which has been under siege from the RSF for more than 18 months, has seen its population rapidly expand to an estimated 3.4 million, about half of whom were displaced by fighting elsewhere.
* Because of the humanitarian implications of this siege, which the UN has warned could become "a repeat of El Fasher" (in which the RSF carried out well-documented atrocities, including door-to-door executions), Egypt is reportedly [pressuring](https://substack.com/redirect/788441f9-b02b-4cd8-af3b-67b1afd29ab0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Sudan's army to accept a ceasefire proposal. Sudanese Army officials believe that the successes of their ongoing operations are sufficient to mitigate this fear, Mada Masr reports.
* **Russian strike on cargo ship kills 10 off Odesa: A Russian missile[ struck](https://substack.com/redirect/c10acc08-254e-4e5b-9702-ed2ea6b374a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a cargo ship shortly after it departed Odesa, killing a Ukrainian port pilot and nine Syrian and** Indian crew members.
* Moscow claimed the vessel carried military cargo, while Ukraine accused Russia of targeting civilian shipping and global food exports.
* Ukrainian authorities say that Russia attacked 23 port facilities and 17 civilian vessels in the first half of July.
* Separately, in Russia, black smoke [blanketed](https://substack.com/redirect/bce318ba-df50-48e5-8bdf-19e6423b9c7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Moscow on Saturday after Ukrainian drones struck logistics warehouses and an oil depot in the area, the AP reported. The Noginsk oil depot, roughly 30 miles east of the capital, holds 24 storage tanks and is a key source of fuel for the region.
* **China and the Philippines trade blame after South China Sea clash:** The Philippine government [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/aa4c3162-1d43-4b37-af74-4fa21604eb46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Chinese Coast Guard personnel beat a Philippine sailor and damaged a navy rubber boat in an encounter between their navies near disputed territory in the South China Sea.
* Beijing claimed the clash was triggered after Philippine vessels ignored warnings, rammed a Chinese patrol boat and attacked Chinese officers first with paddles and wooden poles.
* The clash took place near a disputed maritime shoal claimed by both countries that has become a flashpoint for tensions in recent years as Manila and Beijing compete to assert their authority over portions of the South China Sea.
* **Ecuador bans AMIGO party as electoral purge deepens:** Ecuador's Contentious Electoral Tribunal (TCE) [issued as suspension](https://substack.com/redirect/dc1772dc-0603-4c61-a5d8-16520b2e7cc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against the AMIGO political movement, disqualifying it ahead of November's local elections. The sanction leaves former president Rafael Correa's Revolucion Ciudadana alliance without a viable political vehicle after its main party was previously sidelined. The ruling marks the latest ban of an opposition movement executed without due process. Opposition leaders have condemned the tribunal's decision as a heavy-handed measure designed to dismantle systemic competition and tilt the playing field directly in favor of President Daniel Noboa's political movement.
* Dozens feared dead after passenger ferry sinks off Guyana: Dozens of passengers are [missing](https://substack.com/redirect/0b42c65d-1945-49fc-8512-58aab130ae4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after a ferry carrying 116 passengers and 17 crew members capsized off the coast of Guyana. Authorities rescued 67 people, including 15 children.
* Officials said unlisted passengers were among those rescued, raising questions about the accuracy of the passenger manifest on the ship and leaving authorities uncertain of how many people remain missing.
* Preliminary investigations say that the ferry capsized after being hit by a large wave while sailing towards the Essequibo region.

Iran and Ceasefire U.S. continues its strikes on Iran over the weekend and into Monday: The U.S. several waves of strikes on Iran over the weekend; one attack hit a nuclear power plant. On Saturday, after its eighth consecutive night of strikes, CENTCOM said that it had successfully targeted "Iranian military coastal surveillance and air defense facilities, maritime capabilities, and missile and drone storage sites." The announcement also claimed successful hits on IRGC forces, though no casualty figures were given. The U.S. struck Iran's Darkhovin nuclear power plant on Sunday, according to the country's Atomic Energy Agency. The International Atomic Energy Agency said it would open an investigation into the strike and claimed that the facility was "in the very early stages of construction" and, when it was last visited by the IAEA, "contained no nuclear material." Iran's atomic agency called on the IAEA to directly condemn the strike, which it has yet to do, citing IAEA resolutions declaring that attacks on peaceful nuclear facilities violate international law. U.S. strikes overnight into Saturday 116 telecommunications towers offline, authorities from Iran's Hormozgan province reported, disrupting landline, internet, and mobile service in the region. U.S. attacks on Sunday several areas within Iran including, the city of Abadan, in the southwestern Khuzestan province, the city of Shadegan in the same province, Qeshm Island, and the southern cities of Sirik and Hajiabad in the Hormozgan province. On Monday morning, U.S. strikes were across Iran, from the northern city of Tabriz to the western city of Khorramabad to the southeastern city of Kerman. Additional strikes were reported in the frequently targeted cities of Bushehr and Jask. CENTCOM on Sunday that its blockade of Iran had redirected six commercial vessels and "disabled" one. U.S. strikes have at least 50 and wounded 517 since they restarted strikes on July 6, Iran's Health Ministry reported on Sunday, with 12 of these deaths occurring from Friday to Saturday. Iranian retaliatory attacks: Iranian forces launched retaliatory attacks on U.S. partner nations in the Gulf over the weekend, hitting a number of critical targets. Iran's Revolutionary Guard several successful strikes on U.S. military infrastructure in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan early on Saturday, including strikes on a ground forces support center, a radar installation, a fuel support pier, sites used to support U.S. fighter jets and other aircraft, and signal communications infrastructure. Sirens also sounded at Yanbu, one of Saudi Arabia's principal Red Sea ports and one that has grown more vital during disruptions to traffic through Hormuz. Iran a "vital" oil-sector facility, the Kuwait Petroleum Corporation reported on Saturday, adding that the site was evacuated and that the attack caused "significant material losses." The Iranian army reported two more attacks on U.S. bases in Kuwait on Saturday evening, including on an ammunition depot at Camp Arifjan and the Ali Al Salem airbase. A separate Iranian attack on Sunday a Kuwaiti power generation and water desalination plant, the third consecutive attack confirmed by the country's authorities, though they did not name the facility involved. The attack knocked a "large number" of generating units out of operation, according to Kuwait's Electricity, Water and Renewable Energy Ministry, which condemned the attack as "heinous Iranian aggression." Explosions were in the Iraqi city of Erbil, in the country's Kurdistan region, with drones seen flying over the city, according to Al Mayadeen. The outlet reported that American air defenses were activated in response. Jordan that it shot down three Iranian missiles on Sunday, with a fourth landing in an open area and causing no damage. Some reports suggested damage at or near King Hussein International Airport, where thick black smoke could be seen. Iran on Sunday that it struck two ships that attempted to subvert its authority over the Strip, noting four total incidents in which ships attempted to use a U.S.-designated southern route to transit the Strait and ignored warnings from the Iranian navy, two of which involved the use of military force. Iranian state media also high-resolution satellite images of its weekend attacks on U.S. bases in Bahrain, Jordan, Iraq, Kuwait, and Qatar on Sunday. U.S. confirms deaths of three service members: CENTCOM on Saturday the deaths of two U.S. soldiers in Jordan, killed during an attack on July 17, and reported that one additional soldier remained missing in action, while four had been transported to hospitals to attend to their wounds. The New York Times that U.S. installations in Jordan have come under four waves of attacks in five days, and that these attacks have wounded dozens and inflicted serious damage on American helicopters, with the true casualty count and damage underreported by CENTCOM. The U.S. also on Sunday the death of another soldier in northern Iraq. The soldier was detonating unexploded ordnance from an Iranian drone, CENTCOM claimed, adding that another soldier was wounded in the incident. 17 total American service members have been since the war on Iran began in February, according to the Associated Press. Iran suspends MOU commitments: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi reporters on Saturday that the country would be suspending its obligations under the Islamabad memorandum of understanding, citing Washington's initial violations of the deal. In remarks carried by Iran's Fars News Agency, Gharibabadi accused the United States of having "violated and suspended all its commitments" which the deal obliged it to follow, and said that Iran would move on from the deal and remain "focused on defending the country." Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei a subsequent statement excoriating the U.S. for its "repeated breaches of its commitments" as part of the MOU, and saying these proved "how worthless and unreliable the signature of the U.S. president is," and how "bullying, domination, and savagery are inseparable components of the American way and doctrine." Iran, U.S. signal openness to diplomacy amid ongoing strikes: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday that diplomatic efforts were continuing alongside the military response to U.S. attacks. Speaking at his weekly press conference, Baghaei confirmed that proposals had been conveyed to Iran through intermediaries but declined to disclose their details. Baghaei said Iran's diplomatic apparatus was working in coordination with the armed forces and would "spare no effort to stop the American crimes." Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni, meanwhile, is expected to visit Islamabad on Monday evening to deliver a message from President Masoud Pezeshkian to Pakistan's leadership, according to a Pakistani source cited by Al Jazeera. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio Sunday that Washington remains open to diplomacy but that the MOU could not be considered "alive" while Iran was violating its terms by attacking ships and restricting passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Rubio claimed Iran had sent signals through direct and indirect channels that it wanted to negotiate, but that Washington would continue its military response unless Tehran's conduct changed. Iranian energy ministry announces repairs to Jask water facility complete: Repairs to the Bonji desalination plant were and water service in the area resumed, Iran's energy ministry announced on Sunday, less than 48 hours after the facility was damaged in a U.S. missile strike. The plant supplies drinking water to about 10,000 people across 20 villages in western Jask county. Araghchi says Iran expected war and prepared retaliation before U.S.-Israeli attack: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi a detailed account of the 40-day war, saying Tehran expected war before the conflict began, had prepared contingency plans, and entered last-minute nuclear talks to exhaust diplomacy before what it believed would be a U.S.-Israeli attack. Araghchi said the Supreme National Security Council drew up plans for multiple scenarios, including one codenamed "Code 110" if Iran's leader was killed. The plan called for closing the Strait of Hormuz and launching a broader regional response. Araghchi** said he was inside the leadership compound when multiple buildings were struck, escaping through rubble after three explosions. The coordinated strikes targeted senior military and political leaders and exposed a major "security breach." Read more of Araghchi's extensive comments . Iraq seeks alternative oil transport routes: Iraq plans to two new routes to export its oil, Oil Minister Basem Mohammed Khadir said on Saturday, following major constraints on its export industry due to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. One will involve Turkey's Ceyhan port, and the other will involve Syria's Banyas port, according to state media. Iraq, the second-largest oil producer in OPEC, has received U.S. backing in its effort to rebuild a crude pipeline from Kirkuk through Syria to the Mediterranean, with U.S. companies expected to help construct the pipeline, according to CNBC. The announcement a larger trend, reported on by CNBC on Saturday, of Middle Eastern states, including Iraq and the UAE, seeking to build overland pipelines to bypass disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz. At least 7 of these pipelines are under construction or planned, according to the outlet. The U.S. energy firm HKN Energy on Sunday that it would halt all operations in Iraqi Kurdistan as a result of escalating hostilities in the area, according to the Kurdish outlet Rudaw. HKN recently signed a deal with Iraq to develop the Hamrin field in Salahaddin province, north-central Iraq, targeting output of 140,000 barrels of oil per day and 40 million cubic feet of gas. Lebanon Israeli forces burn and demolish homes in southern Lebanon, despite "ceasefire": Israeli forces to homes in the southern Lebanese town of Kfartebnit on Monday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. In a separate incident, Israeli forces demolitions in the town of Taybeh in the Marjayoun district, the agency reported. Rubio meets Lebanese president in D.C.: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Lebanese President Joseph Aoun at the State Department on Sunday, praising Lebanon's "move toward peace" and pledging U.S. support for "the successful implementation of the Trilateral Framework," the department said. Aoun's office said he would press for talks on strengthening the ceasefire and on "the withdrawal of Israel from the Lebanese regions it occupies." The framework agreement, signed June 26, ties Israeli withdrawal to Hezbollah's disarmament, which Hezbollah has rejected, with no timeframe. Critics have noted that it extracts few guarantees from Israel, which has pledged to stay in the country indefinitely, and loads nearly all of its obligations onto the Lebanese government, which has shown limited ability to assert its authority, especially in the country's south, where Israel continues to violate the ceasefire on an almost daily basis. It is the first visit to Washington by a Lebanese head of state since 2009. He meets Trump on Tuesday. Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the past 24 hours, three Palestinians were killed and 22 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,283 killed, with 173,864 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,158 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,756, while 802 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel bombards Gaza over the weekend: On Friday, Israeli forces killed eight mourners in the Nuseirat refugee camp. Medecins Sans Frontieres that its teams had treated 12 people injured in the Nuseirat funeral massacre, including 7 children, and that three were critically wounded, including a 14-year-old. "This is not a ceasefire," the group said in a statement. Israel 10 Palestinians, including 3 children, in attacks on Gaza overnight into Saturday. An Israeli strike killed a family of five in Gaza City's Al-Nasr neighborhood, while three others were killed in attacks in the Al-Zeitoun neighborhood. On Sunday, an Israeli airstrike on Khan Younis at least one and wounded 10 others, all of whom were displaced and sheltering in the city's Al-Mawasi area, according to local journalist Osama Abu Rabee. Israeli forces later shot and killed a 6-year-old in the same area. Israeli artillery also and killed a woman and her daughter in the Al-Zeitoun neighborhood of Gaza City. Palestinian composer found dead in Gaza City: 28-year-old Palestinian composer Qassem al-Khawaja was dead in his apartment in Gaza City on Saturday. His family alleged that he was targeted by collaborators with the Israeli military and the killing was premeditated. Police said they had found a man--whom they did not name as Al-Khwaja--killed with a sharp object in the area, and announced they were opening an investigation into his murder. Al-Khawaja had built a following by rearranging songs using cooking pots and firewood from his family's kitchen. "Music is also the sound of everyday life, even in the hardest circumstances," he previously wrote. Israeli attacks in the occupied West Bank: Israeli forces two Palestinians on Sunday evening, in Deir Jarir, near Ramallah, including a 26-year-old watching the World Cup Final. At least three others were wounded in the attacks. Fadi Al-Naasan, a 17-year-old who was shot by Israeli forces about a week ago and who underwent a foot amputation as a result of the attack, in Ramallah on Saturday. Al-Naasan was a decorated footballer, playing for the local Al-Mughayyir Club and Palestine's youth national football team. Hamas names Khalil Al-Hayya as new chief: Hamas announced on Monday that it has elected Khalil Al-Hayya as the movement's new head of its political bureau, succeeding Yahya Sinwar, who was killed by the Israeli army in October 2024. Al-Hayya was elected through an internal vote, defeating former Hamas political bureau chief Khaled Meshaal in a run-off. A founding member of Hamas since its establishment in 1987, Al-Hayya has served on the movement's five-member leadership council and has led negotiations with Israel on its behalf. Born in the Gaza Strip in 1960, Al-Hayya has lost three sons in Israeli attacks over the years, including one in an Israeli strike targeting Al-Hayya and other Hamas leaders in Doha in September 2025 and another killed in an Israeli airstrike on Gaza City in May. Two-year-old dies amid chickenpox outbreak in Gaza: Medical staff in Gaza have more than 9,300 cases of chickenpox in Gaza in the past two weeks, according to a correspondent from Al Araby, with a 2-year-old dying from the complications related to the disease on Sunday. Medical sources attributed the outbreak to a "combination of mass displacement, severe overcrowding, severely limited access to clean water, sewage, leakage, waste accumulation," and total collapse of hygiene conditions in Gaza. Dr. Bassam Zaqout, the director of Palestinian Medical Relief, on Sunday that Gaza's health system is nearing a "complete collapse," while Israel continues to destroy medical facilities and restrict the entry of medicines, equipment, and supplies. He pointed to Israel's refusal to allow sodium bicarbonate into the Strip as an example, which is necessary for kidney dialysis treatment, and noted that anemia rates in Gaza had risen from 20% before the war to 50-60% today. Report: Israel holds 16 Palestinian doctors in its prisons: Israel is at least 16 Palestinian doctors in its prisons, the Palestinian Center for Prisoners Advocacy reported on Saturday, where they are subject to torture, starvation, isolation, and medical neglect. The group said the detention retaliation against medical staff who stayed at their post during the genocide in Gaza. It highlighted the cases of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, the director of Kamal Adwan Hospital, who has faced abuse, medical neglect, and threats of retaliation, and Dr. Marwan Al-Hams, who has also been denied medication and contact with his family during the period of his detention. It also noted that the whereabouts of some doctors are deliberately concealed from the public. Palestinian Journalists Syndicate says eight journalists killed, 467 violations recorded in first half of 2026: The Palestinian Journalists Syndicate on Monday via WAFA that Israeli forces and settlers committed 467 violations against Palestinian journalists and media workers during the first half of 2026. The violations included restrictions on reporting, arrests, direct physical attacks, live fire, tear gas, and unfair judicial measures. The report documented the killing of eight journalists during the first six months of the year, bringing the total number killed since October 7, 2023, to 264. According to the report, Israeli forces also carried out 27 arrests of journalists, opened live fire on media crews in 29 incidents, and used tear gas and stun grenades against journalists in 78 cases during the reporting period. U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. NDAA House floor fight over Israeli military fusion: The House of Representatives is expected to vote this week on an amendment from Reps. Thomas Massie and Ro Khanna to strip out a provision that would merge elements of the U.S. and Israeli militaries. Rep. Adam Smith , the top Democrat on the Armed Services Committee, it . The measure was first proposed by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and is understood to be a response to pressure to block U.S. funding for Israel. By integrating the two institutions, it becomes harder for the public to identify specific assistance and pressure their representatives to vote against it. Crypto legislation moving through Senate: The CLARITY Act, backed by the crypto industry, is being pushed toward a Senate floor vote before the August recess, though it currently lacks the Democratic support it would need to overcome a filibuster. (Here's Sen. explaining his objection.) The push comes as Drop Site reports that a major crypto a North Korean hacker. Troy Jackson effectively secures Democratic Senate nomination in Maine: Troy Jackson won than 90% of delegates in county elections held over the weekend to become Maine's replacement Democratic Senate nominee, positioning him to secure the nomination at a July 25 convention in Bangor, Drop Site contributor Nathan Bernard reports. Jackson, a former state senator who leveraged the organizing network of previous nominee Graham Platner , will face Sen. Susan Collins in November after his top rivals, Shenna Bellows and Nirav Shah , dropped out and endorsed him Sunday. Mamdani says Netanyahu arrest still under discussion ahead of UN visit : Mayor Zohran Mamdani in an interview with The New York Times this weekend that his administration is weighing whether to arrest Netanyahu if he visits New York for the U.N. General Assembly in September, saying he is in "active conversation" with the city's Law Department over his legal authority to do so. The Mayor noted Netanyahu's ICC arrest warrant, calling him "a war criminal." Mamdani condemned U.S. policy towards Gaza, saying "It is hard to find a more bankrupt policy approach" than America's conduct towards Gaza and Palestine. Mamdani commented on immigration policy, saying he was "willing to work" with the Trump administration when immigrants were convicted of "serious crimes," but said he refused to participate in civil immigration enforcement operations "with a federal government that has said openly it wants to deport a vast majority of people for crimes that we will never even know." When asked about a possible presidential run from his New York colleague, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez , he said she would "make a good anything." GEO Group employee shoots protester outside Aurora ICE facility : Brandon Booth , a 42-year-old GEO Group employee, was and charged with assault and attempted second-degree murder on Saturday, after police said he shot and wounded a protester Thursday evening outside the Aurora ICE Processing Center in Colorado. Aurora police said Booth fired at two women who were involved in a "verbal confrontation" as part of a protest outside the facility. Booth, who was off-duty, reportedly grabbed his personal pistol and fired a shot in their direction. FBI reportedly stepping back from investigating assaults on ICE agents : The FBI agents in recent days it would stop investigating claims of assaults against Department of Homeland Security agents, a change that would likely shift such cases to ICE's own Homeland Security Investigations division, The New York Times reported on Saturday. In addition to the fact that the change would effectively leave ICE with the responsibility of investigating itself, the Times also notes that these investigations were often sources of valuable information to potential civil rights cases against or prosecutions of ICE agents, a more salient concern in the Trump administration's ongoing violent immigration crackdown. The Justice Department and DHS issued a joint statement denying any policy change. Chicago U.S. attorney 's office in crisis after immigration prosecution failures: The U.S. attorney's office in Chicago has an exodus of veteran prosecutors and lost 59 of 62 federal assault cases brought against immigrants and protesters during last fall's Operation Midway Blitz, The New York Times reported on Sunday, with only one guilty plea and no convictions. More than 100 former federal prosecutors from the office signed a letter criticizing the current U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros , and a judge admonished him this year over his handling of the "Broadview Six" case. "Your sole goal is to do justice," the judge told Boutros in May. She added, "That trust has been broken." Trump order halted federal probe into BAE shipyard harassment claims : A two-year federal investigation into sexual harassment and pay discrimination against women at a BAE Systems shipyard in Norfolk, Virginia, was abruptly after Trump 's January 2025 executive order shut down most work at the Labor Department's Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs, The New York Times reported on Sunday. Investigators, who had documented claims that managers demanded sex acts for overtime and promotions and were nearing a proposed settlement, said the workers never received compensation. The office, which has jurisdiction over approximately 20% of the U.S. workforce, has shrunk from about 480 employees to roughly 75. Trump's budget proposal calls for eliminating it entirely. Rep. Summer Lee, national DSA endorse Donovan McKinney in Detroit: The House Democrat with the most impressive record of choosing primary winners this cycle, Summer Lee , is throwing her weight behind state Rep. Donovan McKinney , who is challenging AIPAC-backed Rep. Shri Thanedar in Michigan. McKinney already had the support of the local Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) chapter, but has now added backing from national. Thanedar, meanwhile, the top three House Democrats. The primary is August 4; last week on Breaking Points. Elizabeth Warren in Michigan Senate race: The Massachusetts senator had been backing Mallory McMorrow before she dropped out. That primary is also August 4. Arizona House primary tomorrow is next chance at incumbent upset: Leftist activist Kai Newkirk is challenging Democratic Rep. Greg Stanton , a leader of the pro-business New Democrat Coalition, in Arizona's 4th congressional district. Polls show the early vote slanted toward Stanton, but with Newkirk surging and performing well among young voters. Other International News Andy Burnham becomes UK prime minister, succeeding Starmer: Andy Burnham was British prime minister on Monday, assuming the position without a challenge after Keir Starmer agreed to step down last month following election defeats and scandals. He has promised to alleviate England's cost-of-living crisis and save its National Health Service, and in his introductory speech, he said his government would pass "power from the authorities to ordinary people." Burnham, who served as mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to 2026 before being elected to Parliament in June, becomes Britain's seventh prime minister in just over a decade. Ansarallah announces maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia: Yemen's Ansarallah an immediate maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, saying it was responding to the kingdom's blockade with a "blockade for blockade." In a statement, the Yemeni Armed Forces said Saudi Arabia had imposed a land, sea and air blockade on Yemen for nearly 12 years, accusing it of plundering the country's resources and saying the latest escalation began with the strike on Sana'a International Airport. The group warned that any further Saudi escalation would be met with a "comprehensive and decisive" response. The announcement follows mass rallies across Yemen and comes after last week it would seek to block Saudi access to the Bab al-Mandab Strait. U.S. to allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium: The Trump administration has a provisional deal that would allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium, CNN reported on Saturday, though Trump himself has not yet signed the deal. The deal, which was negotiated in October 2025, does not require the Kingdom to adopt the IAEA's enhanced safeguards protocol. Sudan updates: Sudan's Army a renewed push in the North Darfur region, particularly on Rapid Support Forces (RSF) positions near the border with Chad, according to Mada Masr, which reported that at least 300 vehicles had crossed the desert into the area in the preceding week. The buildup follows RSF operations in nearby Um Baru, which have affected upwards of 50 towns and villages and displaced over 4,000 people, according to the outlet. An RSF siege on the North Kordofan city of El Obeid the city's main water source, reducing the city's water output by 70 percent, Madr Masr reported on Saturday. The city, which has been under siege from the RSF for more than 18 months, has seen its population rapidly expand to an estimated 3.4 million, about half of whom were displaced by fighting elsewhere. Because of the humanitarian implications of this siege, which the UN has warned could become "a repeat of El Fasher" (in which the RSF carried out well-documented atrocities, including door-to-door executions), Egypt is reportedly Sudan's army to accept a ceasefire proposal. Sudanese Army officials believe that the successes of their ongoing operations are sufficient to mitigate this fear, Mada Masr reports. Russian strike on cargo ship kills 10 off Odesa: A Russian missile a cargo ship shortly after it departed Odesa, killing a Ukrainian port pilot and nine Syrian and Indian crew members. Moscow claimed the vessel carried military cargo, while Ukraine accused Russia of targeting civilian shipping and global food exports. Ukrainian authorities say that Russia attacked 23 port facilities and 17 civilian vessels in the first half of July. Separately, in Russia, black smoke Moscow on Saturday after Ukrainian drones struck logistics warehouses and an oil depot in the area, the AP reported. The Noginsk oil depot, roughly 30 miles east of the capital, holds 24 storage tanks and is a key source of fuel for the region. China and the Philippines trade blame after South China Sea clash: The Philippine government that Chinese Coast Guard personnel beat a Philippine sailor and damaged a navy rubber boat in an encounter between their navies near disputed territory in the South China Sea. Beijing claimed the clash was triggered after Philippine vessels ignored warnings, rammed a Chinese patrol boat and attacked Chinese officers first with paddles and wooden poles. The clash took place near a disputed maritime shoal claimed by both countries that has become a flashpoint for tensions in recent years as Manila and Beijing compete to assert their authority over portions of the South China Sea. Ecuador bans AMIGO party as electoral purge deepens: Ecuador's Contentious Electoral Tribunal (TCE) against the AMIGO political movement, disqualifying it ahead of November's local elections. The sanction leaves former president Rafael Correa's Revolucion Ciudadana alliance without a viable political vehicle after its main party was previously sidelined. The ruling marks the latest ban of an opposition movement executed without due process. Opposition leaders have condemned the tribunal's decision as a heavy-handed measure designed to dismantle systemic competition and tilt the playing field directly in favor of President Daniel Noboa's political movement. Dozens feared dead after passenger ferry sinks off Guyana: Dozens of passengers are after a ferry carrying 116 passengers and 17 crew members capsized off the coast of Guyana. Authorities rescued 67 people, including 15 children. Officials said unlisted passengers were among those rescued, raising questions about the accuracy of the passenger manifest on the ship and leaving authorities uncertain of how many people remain missing. Preliminary investigations say that the ferry capsized after being hit by a large wave while sailing towards the Essequibo region. The second-quarter fundraising numbers are official now, and I want you to see them — because they say just about everything about the two campaigns in this race.
Here's mine: more than 10,000 people chipped in last quarter. 91% of them gave $100 or less, and our average donation was just $15. More than a quarter gave more than once. Together, you helped us out-raise my opponent more than two to one — $1.6 million to his $742,000.
That's not a number I take for granted. That's a movement of working people giving what they can.
Now here's his: nearly half of everything John Braun raised last quarter — 49.7% — came from the national Republican machine. Committees tied to D.C. party bosses. PACs backed by corporations, special interests, and the political elite.
His support from actual people in Southwest Washington has been shrinking for three quarters straight. When the checks from home dried up, the D.C. machine threw him a rope.
That tells you exactly who he'd answer to in Congress. And it tells you exactly who I answer to: you.
I don't take a dime of corporate PAC money — I never have. This campaign only works if people like you keep it going, and with more than $3.9 million banked for the fight ahead, we have real momentum.
Maybe add something about 7 mil reserved against us in TV....
Let's build on it. Will you chip in $5 and keep this a campaign powered by working Washingtonians — not the highest bidder? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]

Thank you for standing with me.

Peter, Last week, President Trump gave a nationally televised speech in which he repeated baseless claims that undermine our elections. In case you missed it, the president spent this time sowing doubt in our elections, and doubled down on the false claim that the 2020 election was rigged in Democrats’ favor. **Casting doubt on the validity of this democratic process is an attack on Americans’ right to choose their elected officials — _and to vote them out. _** So when Republicans lose across the country after ripping away SNAP and healthcare for millions, they can claim it's due to the “negligence” of election officials or voting machine vulnerabilities rather than their poor leadership. And Peter, when powerful voices spread doubt about our voting system, there are very real consequences. _Election workers face threats._ _Voters lose confidence._ _Bad actors use that confusion to roll back protections that keep our communities safe and our rights secure._ **As the people’s lawyer, I won’t let that happen on my watch.** I’ve stood up to President Trump’s unlawful executive order that tried to interfere with states’ constitutional authority to administer elections. I’ve fought to protect mail-in voting and the rights of eligible Washington voters. Small contributions from people like you matter in this fight. Every act of support shows that there’s a coalition of folks ready to stand up for truth, fairness, and the rule of law. **[I need you in this, Peter. clean_body: Trump’s speech, and what it means for upcoming elections: | Peter, Last week, President Trump gave a nationally televised speech in which he repeated baseless claims that undermine our elections. In case you missed it, the president spent this time sowing doubt in our elections, and doubled down on the false claim that the 2020 election was rigged in Democrats’ favor. Casting doubt on the validity of this democratic process is an attack on Americans’ right to choose their elected officials — and to vote them out. So when Republicans lose across the country after ripping away SNAP and healthcare for millions, they can claim it's due to the “negligence” of election officials or voting machine vulnerabilities rather than their poor leadership. And Peter, when powerful voices spread doubt about our voting system, there are very real consequences. Election workers face threats. Voters lose confidence. Bad actors use that confusion to roll back protections that keep our communities safe and our rights secure. As the people’s lawyer, I won’t let that happen on my watch. I’ve stood up to President Trump’s unlawful executive order that tried to interfere with states’ constitutional authority to administer elections. I’ve fought to protect mail-in voting and the rights of eligible Washington voters. Small contributions from people like you matter in this fight. Every act of support shows that there’s a coalition of folks ready to stand up for truth, fairness, and the rule of law. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = = | = = | = = Thank you. — Nick Brown Nick Brown for Attorney General 401 2nd Ave S STE 303 Seattle, WA 98104 United States mailto:info@nickbrownforag.com | Paid for by Nick Brown for Attorney General, DEMOCRAT

name: James Carville, Senior Democratic Strategist
subject: My honest assessment of New Hampshire.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
The math to flip the Senate runs through New Hampshire. Here’s why that should concern you.
Hi. It's James Carville.
I’ve been watching Senate races for decades. What I’m seeing in New Hampshire right now is keeping me up at night — and it should concern y’all too.
I put together a brief memo. Read it. Then let’s help Chris Pappas win this race.
**[If you don’t need convincing, rush a donation to Chris Pappas’s campaign now.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260720_1.FafG1j&refcode=em20260720-1&t=1&akid=7835%2E582294%2EdlTxBF)**
**[Donate »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260720_1.FafG1j&refcode=em20260720-1&t=2&akid=7835%2E582294%2EdlTxBF)**
* * *
**SUMMER 2026 CAMPAIGN MEMO ON NH-SEN**
**FROM:** James Carville, Senior Democratic Strategist
**TO:** Interested Parties
I need to be clear with you about where things stand in the race for New Hampshire’s open Senate seat.
**The New Hampshire Senate race has been in the margin of error for months — and it’s not getting the attention it deserves.**
* Three polls show this race in a dead heat:
* Emerson (March 2026): Pappas 45–Sununu 44
* St. Anselm (March 2026): Pappas 46–Sununu 43
* St. Anselm (November 2025): Pappas 44–Sununu 41
* All of these polls show this race **within the margin of error. The race has been functionally tied for months.**
* New Hampshire’s open Senate seat is sitting in a dead heat with significantly less financial firepower on our side than we have in other Senate races.
* This race will almost certainly be decided by whether Chris Pappas has the resources to compete on the airwaves and on the ground in the final stretch.

**The GOP knows exactly what’s at stake here — and they’re already moving.**
* The Senate Leadership Fund has committed over $17 million to elect John Sununu — their largest investment in New Hampshire in a decade.
* John Sununu is not a back-bench candidate. He has a famous New Hampshire political name (his father and his brother both served as governor), a history of winning statewide, and the full weight of the Republican donor machine behind him.
* And here’s something voters in New Hampshire deserve to know: Sununu left the Senate in 2009 and spent the years following building a personal fortune — with assets estimated as high as $36 million — through corporate board positions and investments in oil and gas companies, including ExxonMobil, Shell, and more. He left New Hampshire, cashed in, and now wants to come back.
* Republicans understand the math perfectly. They don’t need to flip five seats. They just need to flip New Hampshire’s Senate seat and make Democrats’ path to a majority impossible.

**New Hampshire has decided elections before — and the margins are razor thin.**
* In 2016, the last time New Hampshire had a race for an open Senate seat, the race was decided by just 1,017 votes.
* When Democrats chart a path to retaking the Senate majority, New Hampshire is not optional. If Chris Pappas loses, Democrats need to flip five seats instead of four. That math does not exist.

**There is a recent and painful precedent for underestimating a close race.**
* Bob Casey narrowly led in Pennsylvania polling for virtually the entire 2024 cycle — and lost in an upset that shocked the entire party.
* A race that has been tied for six months is not a comfortable position. It is a warning sign. I have seen what happens when we assume a race is in-hand and the resources don’t follow.
* We cannot afford to let New Hampshire’s 2026 race echo Pennsylvania’s in 2024.

**Chris Pappas has what it takes to win — but the outside spending gap is real.**
* Pappas has won New Hampshire’s toughest congressional district four times. He knows how to reach voters across the aisle. His campaign has outraised Sununu candidate-to-candidate with $4.2 million cash on hand to Sununu’s $1.9 million.
* But that advantage disappears the moment the Senate Leadership Fund’s $17 million hits the airwaves. In a race decided by a handful of votes, being drowned out on TV by Republican money in the final weeks is the ballgame.
* This is the moment to make sure New Hampshire doesn’t become the race you wish you’d paid more attention to.

* * *
Listen. The math is simple: Democrats hold New Hampshire, and there’s a path to a majority. Democrats lose it, and nothing else on the map matters.
Chris Pappas needs resources now — before this race gets away from us.
**[Give what you can right now. Let’s win this damn thing and flip control of the Senate.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260720_1.FafG1j&refcode=em20260720-1&t=3&akid=7835%2E582294%2EdlTxBF)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260720_1.FafG1j&amount=5&refcode=em20260720-1&t=4&akid=7835%2E582294%2EdlTxBF)**
– James Carville
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260720_1.FafG1j&refcode=em20260720-1&t=5&akid=7835%2E582294%2EdlTxBF)
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_footer?refcode=em20260720-1&t=6&refcode2=7835_582294_dlTxBF&akid=7835%2E582294%2EdlTxBF)**

Friend — **I’m so excited to share that I will be rallying with my friend Bernie Sanders, as well as Lt. Governor Peggy Flanagan and Attorney General Keith Ellison, tonight in Minneapolis!**
Bernie Sanders has led and grown this progressive movement for years now, inspiring millions of working people, young people, and everyone who has been left behind by the status quo to fight for a better future.
Together at tonight’s The Many Over The Money Rally, we will do everything we can to boost progressive voter turnout and make sure we elect Democrats we can truly believe in here in Minnesota — Democrats who will stand up to Trump, fight for Medicare-for-All, tax the billionaire class, and finally end the era of endless wars.
**So, team, tomorrow marks three weeks until Election Day.**
I can’t stress enough how important the coming days will be, and how important it is that we use every moment to its fullest and raise every dollar that we can for GOTV.
We’ve been running this campaign for months now, but these final days are when many voters are just starting to tune in, and many folks need to be reached by our campaign and get mobilized to go to the polls. So please:
[**As we prepare to rally our movement with Bernie Sanders tonight, will you chip in $10 or anything you can afford to supercharge this campaign and elect progressive leaders up and down the ballot in Minnesota? We need the help of everyone who can pitch in to get the job done.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jul26.gZgURP&refcode=em260720-1-180&t=4&akid=2372%2E791427%2Eaeumto)

name: Elizabeth For Virgina
subject: 15 Days. One Final Ask.
body:
15 days to close the gap

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://us1.campaign-archive.com/?e=2f83c585b2&u=7568ef2270fb76d1ad97da0de&id=5228d3233f)
---
|
---
|
---
| | | | | |
Friends,
In just **15 days** , this campaign comes down to the voters.
Seven months ago, we started with an idea that most people said wasn’t possible. We didn’t have the establishment behind us. We didn’t have corporate PAC money. We didn’t have Dominion writing checks. We didn’t have special interests or political insiders clearing the path.
We had each other.
Together, we’ve built something extraordinary.
We’ve knocked on thousands of doors, made thousands of phone calls, earned the support of people across this district, and grown into one of the **three frontrunners** in this race. We did it while raising less money than the other leading campaigns and after spending months less on the campaign trail than they have.
That didn’t happen because we had the biggest bank account.
It happened because people believed that politics could still belong to ordinary Americans. (And we worked really really hard).
Now we enter the most important 15 days of this election.
The reality is simple: voters can’t choose a candidate they’ve never heard of. These final two weeks are when undecided voters make their decisions, and reaching them through advertising could determine the outcome of this election.
Today, we are **$15,000 short of fully funding our final media buy.**
If we raise that $15,000 over the next 15 days, we will have everything we need to finish this race strong. I truly believe this is the last time I’ll need to ask.
I know times are hard. I know every dollar matters. That’s why I’ve made a promise throughout this campaign: **I will never sell my vote to buy this seat.**
I don’t take money from Dominion.
I don’t take corporate PAC money.
I don’t take money from special interests.
I don’t owe political favors to party insiders.
When I get to Congress, the only people I’ll work for are the people who put me there.
But campaigns like ours only work when ordinary people decide they’re willing to invest in the future they want to see.
So today, I’m asking one last time.
If you believe working families deserve a voice.
If you believe veterans, foster families, teachers, firefighters, and nurses deserve someone who understands their lives.
If you believe integrity is worth fighting for.
Please chip in whatever you can today.
Whether it’s $10, $25, $50, or $100, every contribution helps us reach another voter before Election Day.
Fifteen days from now, we’ll know whether a true grassroots movement can overcome money and the political establishment.
I believe it can.
I believe in this campaign.
Most of all, I believe in all of you.
Let’s finish this together.
With gratitude,
**Elizabeth Dempsey Beggs**
_P.S. Every ad we run over these next 15 days is only possible because someone like you decided to step up. If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to help, this is it. Let’s finish what we started—together._

| | One of my top priorities in Congress is ensuring access to high-quality, affordable health care for people in Northwest Washington. **That means fighting to lower costs for working families, protect Medicare and Medicaid, strengthen rural hospitals, and improve access to care for veterans, seniors, and children.** I am proud to share that our campaign has earned the endorsement of the **Committee to Protect Health Care** , an organization that understands what is at stake in the fight to protect affordable, accessible health care. I believe health care is a right, and I support universal, affordable coverage.
