---

The 100th meridian has always been North America's invisible continental hinge. Running roughly from the Dakotas down through Texas, it marks the point where average annual rainfall drops below twenty inches and the lush eastern ecosystems give way to the semi-arid High Plains and the deserts beyond. What [John Wesley Powell](https://substack.com/redirect/b4f5813b-38f6-4db8-b273-11abc4ece0ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) recognized in the 1870s--that the West was too dry for traditional, rain-fed agriculture--remains painfully relevant today. In fact, the distinction is sharpening: west of the line, the land is drying out; east of it, the nation's population and productive farmland remain heavily concentrated.

West of the 100th meridian, the Jeffersonian ideal of the small, independent farming family was always a gamble against geography. Precipitation is not only sparse but erratic, dependent on mercurial winter snowpack and thunderstorm patterns that can fail for years at a stretch. The agricultural oasis that did emerge was largely an artifact of the Industrial Age: massive federal dams, river diversions, and, most critically, the Ogallala Aquifer. For decades, fossil water allowed center-pivot irrigation to turn the dry plains of Kansas, Nebraska, and the Texas Panhandle into some of the most productive agricultural acres on Earth. But the Ogallala is a non-renewable bank account, and in many places the water table is dropping so fast that the term "traditional farming area" is becoming historical rather than current. As drought cycles intensify and temperatures rise, the West's carrying capacity for conventional row-crop agriculture is contracting. Ranching, which requires fewer inputs per acre than corn or wheat, is already reasserting itself as the more realistic dryland vocation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f2ff006-555c-4dfa-9088-f3d0f84554bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
East of the line, the story is one of reliable bounty. Moisture from the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic meets eastern air currents and falls with seasonal regularity across the Mississippi Basin, the Ohio River Valley, and the Deep South. This is where the bulk of American corn, soy, and cotton is grown without desperate reliance on mining ancient groundwater. It is also where population density soars. The great Eastern metropolitan corridors--from Boston to Washington, from Chicago to Atlanta--sit amid watersheds that can support both agriculture and millions of urban residents. Water is sufficiently plentiful that its scarcity rarely dominates the political imagination the way it does in Phoenix, Las Vegas, or Denver. Consequently, the East houses the majority of the U.S. population and the bulk of its economic infrastructure, while the West remains comparatively empty despite its vast acreage.
West of the 100th meridian, aquifers are not merely water sources; they are lifelines drawn from prehistoric reserves. Unlike the East, where groundwater is generally replenished by reliable rainfall, the aquifers underlying the High Plains, Great Basin, and Southwest are largely non-renewable on human timescales. The most consequential is the Ogallala Aquifer, the vast subterranean lake stretching beneath portions of South Dakota, Nebraska, Colorado, Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, and New Mexico. For decades it has allowed irrigated corn, wheat, and cotton to flourish on arid land, but in many regions--especially the Texas Panhandle and western Kansas--the water table is plummeting by several feet per year in some places. Extraction routinely exceeds natural recharge by orders of magnitude.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.9zPDNdgYYaf9TXtUzdJl3w97ihd_I1j8Ti930wuhEj0?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=207722078)

Elsewhere, the Edwards-Trinity, Dakota, and Basin and Range aquifers serve cities, ranchlands, and industry across Wyoming, Utah, Arizona, and New Mexico. These systems, too, are shrinking under the pressure of agricultural pumping, municipal demand, and now drought-deepened by climate change. In the Central Valley of California and around Phoenix, groundwater withdrawal has caused measurable land subsidence, permanently reducing aquifer storage capacity.

The fundamental reality is geological. Much of the West's aquifer recharge depends on mountain snowmelt percolating through limited river corridors, a supply that is erratic and, in recent decades, diminishing. Where Eastern aquifers function like bank accounts with steady deposits, Western aquifers are being mined like coal seams--finite buffers against an arid climate. Once depleted, the agricultural productivity and population capacity they sustain will contract sharply, underscoring why the 100th meridian remains a hydrological border between renewable abundance and fossil scarcity.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8df5219b-c949-4cb5-a534-f0781722fc5a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The demographic implication is stark. Americans continue to cluster east of the 100th meridian because that is where the water is. Western growth has occurred in spite of aridity, not because it was overcome; it exists through heroic, expensive, and increasingly fragile hydraulic engineering. As climate change pushes the effective dry line eastward and aquifers deplete, the historic farming areas of the West face an existential squeeze. Meanwhile, the wetter East retains both the soil moisture and the human capital that have always defined national power.

The AI boom is pushing massive data center development into two of the driest corners of the United States, sharpening a tension between digital infrastructure and water scarcity.

Utah sits on the arid edge of the Great Basin, where drought and the shrinking Great Salt Lake already dominate policy debates. Data centers in the state are prodigious water consumers: the NSA facility in Bluffdale used more than 126 million gallons in a single year, while Aligned Data Centers locations in West Valley and West Jordan consumed 80 million and 47 million gallons respectively over the same period. Meta's Eagle Mountain campus more than doubled its water withdrawals between 2021 and 2024, reaching 35 million gallons annually. Proposed projects, including a controversial Box Elder County development, have raised alarms over allocations of several million gallons per day. In response, Utah has enacted new transparency rules requiring developers to report estimated water use before construction begins, but critics argue the state is gambling its limited freshwater on tax-break-heavy tech hubs.

West Texas faces an even drier reality. In the Permian Basin around Midland and Odessa, annual rainfall is sparse and aquifers are stressed. A University of Texas study projects that data centers statewide could claim 9% of Texas water use by 2040--much of it indirectly through thermoelectric power generation. Yet West Texas is pioneering an unusual solution: treated produced water, the toxic, hypersaline byproduct of oil and gas drilling. Because the Permian generates vast volumes of this wastewater, developers and policymakers are promoting its desalination and reuse for server cooling. Major projects, including OpenAI-linked developments, are exploring the model. The state has only recently begun collecting comprehensive water-use data from facilities.
In both regions, the contradiction is stark: some of America's thirstiest industries are expanding where water is least abundant. Utah is clamping down on freshwater disclosures, while West Texas is betting on turning fossil-fuel waste into a digital-age resource.

In short, the 100th meridian still divides two Americas: one where water is an assumed foundation of life and agriculture, and another where its absence dictates every calculation. The West may be mythologized as the frontier of limitless expansion, but its drying landscape is quietly enforcing limits that the wet, populous East does not face.

Despite promises to lower costs, the Trump administration’s decisions have made everyday essentials more expensive — from groceries and gas to health care, utilities, and housing. Martin has been fighting to lower costs and stand up for working families across our state. He recently led a roundtable with Senate colleagues focused on energy policies that are driving up utility bills. name: Troy Jackson
subject: I’m ready to defeat Susan Collins in November. Are you with me?
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Mainers have spoken: I am incredibly proud to be their choice for Democratic nominee in our U.S. Senate race.
My name is Troy Jackson. Growing up in Allagash, I didn’t think I’d ever be anything other than a fifth-generation logger. And for a long time, that was more than enough.
But then I got a political education. Not in some Ivy League university — when I was working in the North Woods, grinding out 80-hour workweeks under the thumb of a billionaire. In those woods I discovered the truth: working class people in this country aren’t struggling to get by because we’re not trying hard enough, or not smart enough, or not anything enough. We’re getting crushed by a rigged system, and we have been for way too long.
I got into politics after a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages.
I stayed because once I was there, it was clear that nobody in power understood the actual hardships I’d been living my whole life. Working class people deserve to have someone who lives these struggles in rooms where decisions are being made.
Since then I’ve fought to lower the cost of prescription drugs, pass universal school meals, expand rural healthcare, protect abortion rights, and deliver tax relief. And we’ve won a lot of those fights. But there’s always been someone with more power stepping in to water down or block our progress, or dictate just how far we could go. Now, with her primary quickly approaching, Kaela's campaign is counting on us to help raise $10,000 by July 31 to reach the voters she needs to win. = = | = Kaela knows what it is like to live paycheck to paycheck and make impossible choices between paying the bills and putting food on the table. name: Deb Haaland
subject: Jars of salsa
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=11088%2E400544%2ECBpdqi)
---
Friend, long before I served in Congress or as Secretary of the Interior, I made a living selling jars of my homemade salsa. I’d prepare my salsa and deliver jars to mom-and-pop shops across the state, often with Somáh riding with me in the back seat.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12770?refcode=jtk1031-fr-nd&t=2&akid=11088%2E400544%2ECBpdqi)
_Here’s Somáh posing with jars of my homemade salsa._
While I started my salsa company because I didn't have access to childcare, I also loved being my own boss, seeing my salsa fill the shelves all over New Mexico, and sharing my homemade recipe.
I also learned firsthand how difficult it is to start a small business. From permits and paperwork to long waits for answers and setting up the right bank accounts, it often felt like there was one hurdle after another.
**I’m committed to making that process easier.** When New Mexicans have a dream for a business, I want to ensure they have the support they need to turn that dream into a reality.
As part of my plan to make life better for all New Mexicans, I will launch an Office of Small Business. This office will coordinate development programs, fill the gaps created by Trump’s funding cuts, and provide a centralized, online platform for grants, capital, and other resources to help businesses get off the ground.
Small businesses make New Mexico special. From handmade salsas to family-owned restaurants, our state is built by fierce problem-solvers and an unstoppable entrepreneurial spirit! **[If you're ready for a leader who will fight for working families, please contribute $5 or whatever you’re able to fuel my campaign.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12770?refcode=jtk1031-fr-nd&t=3&akid=11088%2E400544%2ECBpdqi)**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12770?refcode=jtk1031-fr-nd&t=4&akid=11088%2E400544%2ECBpdqi)
---
Thank you for being in this fight with me.
Be fierce,
Deb

He helped make Montana debt-free. He is tough, he is proven, and he is exactly who we need in the United States Senate. Chuck Schumer and his allies raised $130 million in a single month through ActBlue with Montana in their sights. Chuck knows that if he flips Montana, he takes back the Senate. That’s why I am reaching out to you today with a simple ask: I’ve sat down with Kurt and I know he is trustworthy and will protect our shared values. He believes what we believe - securing the border, lowering taxes, fighting for voter ID laws, and supporting President Trump's America First agenda. I have met many candidates over the years and I know that Kurt Alme is the real deal. Schumer is on the move. The fight over it has brought Congress to a standstill -- other legislation blocked outright to force the Senate's hand. The House is going again before the August recess. That is the window. If it does not become law, the 2026 election runs under the same rules we have right now. That is the whole fight. -- The 2026 Victory Team P.S. The Senate stalled it once already. ---
**Testosterone Screening Is Preventive Medicine for the US Military** By Bobby Jindal and Keith Kellogg
---
Just a few days ago, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said, “We owe our warriors the absolute best medical care in the world, and this program delivers on that obligation.”

On the medicine, he is right. Under the July 15 directive, “all Active Duty and Reserve Component personnel aged 30 and older” will have testosterone measured once a year as part of the Periodic Health Assessment they already sit for. Troops under 30 may request the test. If a result comes back low and a military physician recommends treatment, the service member decides whether to accept it.

The problem, “low T,” has a military history that predates this Pentagon and this administration. In 2020, the International Journal of Psychiatry in Medicine described “Operator Syndrome”, the various medical and behavioral conditions produced by the extraordinary wear and tear of a career in special operations. Hormonal dysfunction sits on that list alongside traumatic brain injury, sleep disturbance, chronic pain, and depression. The conclusion? Blast exposure and chronic stress dysregulate the endocrine system, and low testosterone shows up as fatigue, low mood, poor concentration, and disrupted sleep.

And this is not, as some coverage implied, a program for men only. Hegseth said “service member,” not “serviceman.” That matters because testosterone is not a male-only hormone. Women produce it too, and clinical evidence ties low levels in women to diminished energy, mood, cognition, and bone density, while supplementing with low doses of testosterone is linked with healthy aging in women.

clean_body: | | | Testosterone Screening Is Preventive Medicine for the US Military By Bobby Jindal and Keith Kellogg Just a few days ago, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said, “We owe our warriors the absolute best medical care in the world, and this program delivers on that obligation.” On the medicine, he is right. Under the July 15 directive, “all Active Duty and Reserve Component personnel aged 30 and older” will have testosterone measured once a year as part of the Periodic Health Assessment they already sit for. Troops under 30 may request the test. If a result comes back low and a military physician recommends treatment, the service member decides whether to accept it. The problem, “low T,” has a military history that predates this Pentagon and this administration. In 2020, the International Journal of Psychiatry in Medicine described “Operator Syndrome”, the various medical and behavioral conditions produced by the extraordinary wear and tear of a career in special operations. Hormonal dysfunction sits on that list alongside traumatic brain injury, sleep disturbance, chronic pain, and depression. The conclusion? Blast exposure and chronic stress dysregulate the endocrine system, and low testosterone shows up as fatigue, low mood, poor concentration, and disrupted sleep. And this is not, as some coverage implied, a program for men only. Hegseth said “service member,” not “serviceman.” That matters because testosterone is not a male-only hormone. Women produce it too, and clinical evidence ties low levels in women to diminished energy, mood, cognition, and bone density, while supplementing with low doses of testosterone is linked with healthy aging in women. | | Email sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com by AmericaNext

I wanted to send a different kind of email today to take a step back and
tell you a little bit more about why I decided to run for governor of
Michigan.

My decision to run — and most choices I’ve made in my life — all stem from
one belief: I believe everyone deserves a fair shot in life.

Growing up in a middle class family as the daughter of two special
education teachers, the values of hard work, opportunity, and serving
others were instilled in me at an early age.

I always knew I wanted to fight for justice and make a difference.

It’s why I started my career investigating threats to democracy and civil
rights. Then I served as a law clerk to a federal civil rights judge in
Detroit, protecting and defending people’s civil rights and freedoms.
Then, as Dean of Wayne State University Law School, I worked to make sure
all students could afford their education by freezing tuition and
expanding scholarships.

It’s why, as Secretary of State, I’ve fought to make everyday life easier
for all Michiganders, secure our elections, and expand voter access.

But our work is far from finished. I’m running for governor
to make sure Michigan is a place where everyone — from our kids to our
seniors — can live and thrive.

But Michigan is one of the most competitive states in the country, and the
latest polls show this race is going to be extremely close. Winning here
won’t be easy... or cheap.

I’m committed to building a campaign built by the people, for the people.
While my Republican counterpart has already accepted $5 million from the
DeVos family funneled into a shady super PAC, [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/9464?t=1003&akid=1733%2E181023%2E4z01YL ]our campaign is building
real momentum, and we can’t let it stall. So please, if you can: will

| | **_Meet Rob:_** Born and raised in Kingston, PA, Rob Bresnahan is currently serving his first term as PA-08’s homegrown Congressman. He’s a fifth-generation Northeastern Pennsylvanian, and the only representative in Congress who is part of the National Electrical Contractors Association. A product of the American Dream, Rob learned the true meaning of hard work by getting his hands dirty early and often. He wired junction boxes, ran heavy equipment, drove trucks, and learned the value of an honest day’s work in the process. His family instilled the values of hard work, discipline, and perseverance in him at a young age – and Rob has stayed true to these foundational values all his life. At just 19 years old, Rob joined his family’s business as the CFO for Kuharchik Construction. He became the CEO of the company in 2013. Rob spent over a decade working and connecting with blue-collar Americans across the country before running for Congress in 2024. He was outspent 2:1 in his race against a 12-year Democrat that year, but the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania demanded change when they sent Rob to be their fighter in Washington. Through his experience as an electrical contractor, Rob saw the real world struggles facing America’s blue-collar workers first hand. Wages are not keeping up with the skyrocketing cost of living, and Americans who wake up every day and pay their dues are being left out to dry by their elected officials. But Rob’s voting record in Congress tells a different story. He’s stood up for hardworking Americans at every opportunity, regardless of partisan politics. Simply put, Rob Bresnahan brings both insight and candid concern for blue-collar America to Congress that your run-of-the-mill representatives don’t. Every day that he steps foot on Capitol Hill, Rob is 100% devoted to restoring America’s energy independence, deregulating the economy, and bringing well-paying jobs back to the great commonwealth of Pennsylvania. While he’s still serving his freshman term in Congress, Rob has already introduced key legislation to re-invest in American trades and pave avenues to success for young people who forgo a traditional college education. Now running for re-election in one of the most pivotal battleground races in the country, Rob is stepping up to the plate once again to deliver for the people of PA-08 and preserve our Republican House majority for the remainder of President Trump’s second term.

body:
Join our community call on Tuesday, July 21 | | | Peter, The Administration is carrying out the largest mass delegalization effort in modern U.S. history, and working families are paying the price. As more of our neighbors lose their ability to work, entire communities are pushed into an affordability crisis. DACA renewal delays and court decisions are making it easier to detain and deport recipients. Federal agents have detained over 340 DACA recipients and deported at least 90 since the start of 2025. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court’s decision on Haitian and Syrian TPS is stripping protection from 1.5 million TPS holders. But we don't have to be in this chaos. clean_body: Join our community call on Tuesday, July 21 | | | Peter, The Administration is carrying out the largest mass delegalization effort in modern U.S. history, and working families are paying the price. As more of our neighbors lose their ability to work, entire communities are pushed into an affordability crisis. DACA renewal delays and court decisions are making it easier to detain and deport recipients. Federal agents have detained over 340 DACA recipients and deported at least 90 since the start of 2025. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court’s decision on Haitian and Syrian TPS is stripping protection from 1.5 million TPS holders. But we don't have to be in this chaos. The solution exists, and we need you with us to fight for it. Rep. Sylvia Garcia has filed a discharge petition on the full Dream and Promise Act (H.R. 1589), which would provide a pathway to citizenship for over 4.4 million immigrant young people, DACA recipients, and TPS holders. If 218 Members of Congress add their name to the discharge petition, the bill goes directly to the House floor for a vote. This is an opportunity for Members of Congress to show up for everyday working people: the millions of people who work, pay taxes, raise families, and keep this country running. **We'll break down what is the Dream and Promise Act, what a discharge petition is, and why it's an important opportunity in our work for citizenship for millions, and how people around the country will be coming together to get the support of 218 Members of Congress for the Dream and Promise Act. Then we'll take action together: we'll call Congress live during the call and make a plan to keep the pressure on all summer. ** In unity, The United We Dream team | Follow us on: | | | | |

**I had the opportunity to sit down with several active AARP members from Connecticut to discuss the issues that matter most to them --not only as AARP members, but as constituents, seniors, caregivers, and families planning for retirement.**
[Pledge your support](https://substack..GTMz80B1fH3ppj6c73tGjY7xfPqThcMQv-ZdBEiHU_w?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=207843678)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=207843678&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA3ODQzNjc4LCJpYXQiOjE3ODQ1ODcwNjUsImV4cCI6MTc4NzE3OTA2NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.yJapInbUIihY6ijbnejz9sMUG49WLvAUir9knDhyncY)
As an AARP member myself, I appreciated the thoughtful and productive conversation. What made it especially meaningful was that we weren't simply discussing politics--we were sharing personal experiences.
_Those experiences often lead to the best public policy because they reflect the real challenges families face every day._
As a physician, attorney, current member of the Greenwich Representative Town Meeting (RTM) **Health and Human Services Committee** , and former family caregiver, I have seen many of these challenges from multiple perspectives. Those experiences have shaped my views on healthcare, aging, Social Security, and long-term care.
> _Throughout my career, I have learned that the best solutions rarely come from political slogans. They come from listening, asking questions, studying the facts, and understanding how government policies affect real people._
**Protecting and Strengthening Social Security**
Let me be clear:
**I fully support Social Security.**
Social Security is not a government handout. It is an earned benefit that millions of Americans paid into throughout their working lives. The Federal Government has a responsibility to honor that commitment.
Before Congress raises taxes, reduces benefits, or significantly increases the retirement age, we should first examine how Social Security has been managed.
As I discussed in my article, **"[ Social Security: Before Raising Taxes, Manage the Money Better,](https://open.substack.com/pub/drmichaelgoldstein4ct/p/social-security-before-raising-taxes?r=26c3ku&utm_medium=ios)"** we should focus on improving the stewardship of the Social Security Trust Fund before asking hardworking Americans to contribute even more.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f1b71e2b-4228-4a71-b806-fceeed6022bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Read the full article here:**
[https://open.substack.com/pub/drmichaelgoldstein4ct/p/social-security-before-raising-taxes?r=26c3ku&utm_medium=ios](https://open.substack.com/pub/drmichaelgoldstein4ct/p/social-security-before-raising-taxes?r=26c3ku&utm_medium=ios)
Too often, the debate begins with raising payroll taxes or reducing benefits. I believe Congress should first ask whether the existing funds are being managed in the most responsible way possible.
I support:
* Protecting benefits for today's retirees.
* Preserving Social Security for future generations.
* Greater transparency and accountability in the management of the Social Security Trust Fund.
* Responsible long-term investment strategies that strengthen the Trust Fund while maintaining appropriate safeguards.
* Preserving the connection between what workers contribute and the benefits they ultimately receive.
* Avoiding dramatic increases in the retirement age.

**As a physician, I also recognize that retirement is not the same for everyone.**
> Someone who has spent forty years working in construction, manufacturing, transportation, nursing, public safety, or another physically demanding profession often cannot continue working into their late sixties or seventies simply because their body has endured decades of wear and tear.
Public policy should recognize those realities.
**Supporting Family Caregivers**
One of the strongest themes from our discussion was support for family caregivers.
This issue is deeply personal to me.
> My family and I have cared for aging relatives, coordinated medical care, navigated rehabilitation facilities and nursing homes, and experienced firsthand the emotional, financial, and physical demands placed upon families caring for loved ones.
Those experiences taught me something that statistics alone never can.
Family caregivers are the backbone of long-term care in America.
They sacrifice careers, income, retirement savings, vacations, weekends, and countless hours caring for parents, spouses, and relatives because they love them.
Yet too often, they receive little recognition or support.
I believe we should seriously explore:
* Tax credits for eligible family caregivers.
* Direct financial assistance for lower-income caregivers.
* Assistance with transportation, mileage, home modifications, medical equipment, and caregiving expenses.
* Respite care so caregivers can continue working and maintain their own health.
* Training and educational resources for family caregivers.
* Expanded physician home visits and home-based healthcare.
* Carefully designed pilot programs that identify the most effective and cost-efficient caregiving models before expanding them nationwide.

Supporting family caregivers is not only compassionate--it is also smart public policy.
**My Experience on the RTM Health and Human Services Committee**
Serving on the Greenwich RTM Health and Human Services Committee gave me a greater appreciation for the tremendous challenges facing seniors, families, healthcare providers, and taxpayers.
I see firsthand the growing costs associated with long-term care, rehabilitation services, transportation, healthcare access, and nursing-home placement.
Quality nursing facilities provide an essential service and will always be necessary for many individuals. However, they should not automatically become the default solution.
Today, **nursing-home care can cost between $10,000 and $20,000 per month** , creating enormous financial pressure on families. When personal savings are exhausted, Medicaid often becomes responsible for those costs, increasing the burden on taxpayers.
> Beyond the financial considerations, there are important quality-of-life issues. A family member who sees an aging parent every day often notices subtle changes in memory, appetite, mobility, or overall health long before they become medical emergencies.
That kind of daily observation cannot always be duplicated in an institutional setting.
Early intervention frequently prevents hospitalizations, improves outcomes, and allows seniors to remain independent longer.
**Expanding Alternatives to Nursing Homes**
Whenever medically appropriate, we should expand alternatives that allow seniors to remain safely in their own homes and communities.
These include:
* Home healthcare.
* Physician home visits.
* Adult day health programs.
* Respite care.
* Home safety modifications.
* Remote health-monitoring technology.
* Better coordination between family caregivers and healthcare providers.

These alternatives often improve quality of life while reducing healthcare costs.
Rather than immediately placing someone into institutional care, we should ask whether there is a better solution that allows them to remain with family while maintaining their dignity and independence.
Government should encourage innovation by testing new approaches through pilot programs, measuring outcomes, and expanding the programs that demonstrate better care and lower costs.
**Experience Leads to Better Solutions**
One lesson from our conversation stood out.
_**The best ideas often come from people who have actually lived through these experiences.**_
As a physician, I have treated patients from every socioeconomic background.
As an attorney, I have worked through complex legal and healthcare issues.
As a member of the RTM Health and Human Services Committee, I have examined the public policy challenges facing our communities.
As a family caregiver, I understand the emotional and financial realities that families experience every day.
Those experiences have taught me that good public policy begins with listening.
Government should spend less time arguing over partisan talking points and more time listening to the people who actually live these issues.
**My Two Commitments**
**1\. I Fully Support Social Security.**
Americans earned these benefits through a lifetime of work, and we must protect and strengthen Social Security while improving the long-term management of the Trust Fund so future generations can rely on it as well.
**2\. I Strongly Support Family Caregivers.**
Families who care for aging loved ones deserve meaningful support. By expanding home-based care, recognizing caregivers, and creating practical alternatives to institutional nursing-home placement, we can improve quality of life for seniors while making better use of taxpayer dollars.
These are not Republican issues or Democrat issues.
They are American issues.
I appreciated the opportunity to meet with Connecticut's AARP members, listen to their concerns, exchange ideas, and continue a conversation centered on dignity, affordability, independence, and keeping our promises to America's seniors.
**I Would Be Honored to Earn Your Support**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e946e2c-f93f-4d84-bdea-53ec7d817ca5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I would be honored to earn the support of **AARP members, seniors, and everyone approaching retirement age throughout Connecticut.**
Our conversations reinforced my belief that good public policy begins by listening to those with real-life experience. As a physician, attorney, current RTM Health and Human Services Committee member, family caregiver, and fellow AARP member, I am committed to protecting Social Security, supporting family caregivers, and advancing practical, affordable alternatives that help seniors live with dignity, independence, and security.
**For registered Republicans, I would be honored to earn your vote in the Republican Primary on August 11. Early voting begins August 3 and continues through August 9.**
Together, we can bring practical experience, thoughtful leadership, and common-sense solutions to Washington on behalf of Connecticut's seniors, families, and future retirees.
To learn more, please visit **[www.goldsteinforcongress.com](https://substack.com/redirect/318fbc49-24e0-4812-a4d8-31f20fcf8bc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
Thank you to Connecticut's AARP members for the opportunity to listen and learn. I look forward to continuing these conversations across our state because the best policies are built by listening first--and leading with experience, compassion, and common sense.

A federal judge refused to block Donald Trump’s executive order to create a federal voter list and limit mail voting.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
That means the fight to protect free, fair, and accessible elections just suffered a blow — and the stakes could not be higher.
Trump and his allies are still trying to sow distrust in our elections, restrict access to the ballot box, and give the federal government unprecedented control over how Americans vote. They’re targeting vote-by-mail even after repeated audits and investigations confirmed there was no widespread fraud in the 2020 election.
And make no mistake: this is exactly why we need everyone on board, fighting back harder than ever to save our democracy and the rule of law.
In Oregon, we know vote-by-mail works. We’ve spent decades building a system that is secure, accessible, and trusted by voters across the political spectrum. But national attacks on voting rights don’t stop at state borders.
As Secretary of State, I’ll do everything in my power to protect Oregon voters, defend election workers from political intimidation, and ensure our elections remain free from partisan interference.
But I can’t do this alone. We to prove that Oregonians are ready to stand together against these attacks on democracy. Will you chip in before midnight to help me continue this fight? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
The courts may not have stopped this latest attack yet — but voting rights advocates are continuing the legal battle, and we must continue organizing, mobilizing, and preparing for what comes next.
This campaign is about protecting democracy itself. And it will take all of us working together to win.
Thank you,

name: Mary Peltola
subject: First poll showing us down >>
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Maggie for NH
body:
We need to respond | There have been six polls in the six months since I launched this campaign for Alaska’s U.S. Senate seat. We were leading in the first five.

Then, after my opponent and the billionaires and super PACs that back him started spending millions on attack ads against me, **the New York Times/Siena University poll released this month shows us down two points.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135649407/634915501/-328725030?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.20_Mary-Peltola-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP-NC_RS-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMTMzMDA2Yi04ZDg0LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=77d9UYiHD4BLefIpjgILCXydVsJcRQhQrQVHPqn0eOk=) We need your help to respond.

**Election forecasters like Cook Political Report, Sabato’s Crystal Ball, Split Ticket, and VoteHub have all called Alaska’s U.S. Senate race a toss-up.**

They shifted the race in our favor because they know we can win, and that all eyes are on Alaska this year in what’s shaping up to be the most competitive and consequential race on the Senate map.

They know we can win because Alaskans are fed up with the rigged system that’s pricing us out and threatening our way of life while DC politicians and their donors make themselves richer.

They know we can win because my opponent, Dan Sullivan, is the least popular senator up for reelection, and Alaskans want someone who will fight for their healthcare, jobs, disaster relief, and public media – not gut them.

They know we can win because I’ve won Alaska statewide – twice – against our former governor Sarah Palin, and now we’re building a movement that’s ready to take on the rigged DC system so we can lower costs, save our fisheries, and bring abundance back to our state.

**They know we can win this toss-up Senate race if we can raise the resources needed to overcome the attack ads and get our message out.**

Our fight for fish, family, and freedom resonates in every region of our big, beautiful state – _and in a state as big as Texas, Montana, and California combined, that’s a pretty broad coalition!_

We’re criss-crossing as much of Alaska’s 586,000 square miles as we can to bring every village and every voter into our campaign, and we’re doing all we can to fight back with ads online and on the airwaves.

**But this is without a doubt the most expensive state on the map to run a Senate campaign. To win in Alaska means building a strong ground game and winning the screen war – reaching communities on and off the road system, from the Aleutians to Anchorage to the Arctic.**

No one ever said flipping Alaska’s Senate seat was going to be easy. But we do know that this is our best chance to do it. They shifted the race in our favor because they know we can win, and that all eyes are on Alaska this year in what’s shaping up to be the most competitive and consequential race on the Senate map. They know we can win because Alaskans are fed up with the rigged system that’s pricing us out and threatening our way of life while DC politicians and their donors make themselves richer. They know we can win because my opponent, Dan Sullivan, is the least popular senator up for reelection, and Alaskans want someone who will fight for their healthcare, jobs, disaster relief, and public media – not gut them. They know we can win because I’ve won Alaska statewide – twice – against our former governor Sarah Palin, and now we’re building a movement that’s ready to take on the rigged DC system so we can lower costs, save our fisheries, and bring abundance back to our state. They know we can win this toss-up Senate race if we can raise the resources needed to overcome the attack ads and get our message out. Our fight for fish, family, and freedom resonates in every region of our big, beautiful state – and in a state as big as Texas, Montana, and California combined, that’s a pretty broad coalition! We’re criss-crossing as much of Alaska’s 586,000 square miles as we can to bring every village and every voter into our campaign, and we’re doing all we can to fight back with ads online and on the airwaves. # [Carville: Haley's raisin' hell in Michigan - I need you to get off the sidelines and get in the ring with her.](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=207807772&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA3ODA3NzcyLCJpYXQiOjE3ODQ1ODg2MjEsImV4cCI6MTc4NzE4MDYyMSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.asVYEXsyHTsy15AHXu_gyKuXWKgmFXo4wvnrQ47eVP0)
### If you care at all about winning back the Senate majority, now's the time to get in this.
Jul 20
---

---
| | | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/carville-haleys-raisin-hell-in-michigan?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA3ODA3NzcyLCJpYXQiOjE3ODQ1ODg2MjEsImV4cCI6MTc4NzE4MDYyMSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.asVYEXsyHTsy15AHXu_gyKuXWKgmFXo4wvnrQ47eVP0&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)

---

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6d3d6548-44b1-45e1-9524-cea8f0e71a3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Folks, let me ask you something:
Are you sick and tired of Trump's MAGA minions running roughshod over every value our nation claims to hold dear? Of them doing their darndest to strip our rights away right in front of our eyes? Of watching our nation's progress get dragged backward by the crackpot GOP?
Yes?
_THEN WHAT ARE YOU WAITING FOR?_
There's a clear path to stopping the extremist GOP in its tracks and turning Trump's second term into the lamest lame-duck presidency this country's ever seen.
**And that path runs through Michigan.**
Right now, Haley Stevens is in the fight of her life.
She's raising hell and working around the clock to make sure Michigan stays blue so Democrats have more than a snowball's chance in hell of flipping the Senate in November, and let me tell you: She's really up against it.
Now, if you know one thing about me, it's that I've been doing this for so long that I make dirt look young. So when I tell you that the kind of money being thrown into beating Haley is historic, it's something you can take to the bank.
Her opponents are spending eye-watering amounts of money to take down her momentum - and she needs some serious muscle to help her fight back.
There's a real reason for all this crazy spending. The GOP knows that if Haley wins her primary, Trump's handpicked darling for Michigan, Mike Rogers, is going straight back to Florida, where he came from.
**And if Haley beats Rogers in November like we ALL know she can, they kiss their chances at keeping the Senate majority goodbye.**
That's not something they're going to leave to chance.
But if they think Democrats like me are going to roll over and let them have Michigan, they've got another thing coming.
I'm jumping into this race right alongside Haley because I know she's got what it takes to bring home the win, not just for Michigan but for all of us. And I need you to get off the sidelines and get in this with us, folks.
**I 'll cut to the chase: The next big deadline for Haley's campaign is tomorrow at midnight. She needs to blow this thing out of the water, and to do that, she needs YOU. [Will you rush $10 NOW to help her hit her $50,000 goal so we can flip the Senate blue and stop the MAGA madness?](https://substack.com/redirect/6d3d6548-44b1-45e1-9524-cea8f0e71a3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c5aef32c-e97b-4b2c-b723-248d95fa64ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I'm counting on you. Haley is counting on you. Michigan is counting on you.
Now let's give 'em hell.
James Carville

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c5aef32c-e97b-4b2c-b723-248d95fa64ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

subject: Judicial Watch: FBI Received Faxes ‘Claiming Credit’ for TWA Flight 800 — New Documentary Marks 30th Anniversary
body:
Judicial Watch announced today that it received 415 pages of records in a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) which show the Bureau received faxes claiming credit for the July 1996 explosion of Trans World Airlines (TWA) Flight 800.

name: Mark Teixeira
subject: Hill Country Floods: Standing With Our Fellow Texans
body:
Recovery resources are available—and every act of support can make a difference.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/t5F2dhL2Yh8?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Peter,
It’s heartbreaking to see the Texas Hill Country facing **devastating floods** once again.
Right now, the immediate priority is making sure people receive the help they need. If you’re in or near the affected area, please **continue checking on your friends and neighbors** —especially the elderly and anyone who may have difficulty getting help on their own. Find out whether they need assistance reaching a shelter, reporting damage, or connecting with recovery services.
Several [**resources are available**](https://us.list-manage.com/yqR5woCxH1m?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)**** for those seeking assistance and those who want to [**volunteer**](https://us.list-manage.com/KuIEjC9IVEN?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592). Please review the information below and share it with anyone who may need help.
It’s always inspiring to see **Texans stand strong** and step up for one another when disaster strikes. Thank you to the first responders, volunteers, local leaders, Governor Abbott, Congressman Roy, and the many others working around the clock to support these communities.
I’m making a $250,000 donation through my foundation to support flood relief efforts. If you’re able, I hope you’ll [**join me in giving what you can**](https://us.list-manage.com/1BUtf556sG8?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)**** to help our fellow Texans recover and rebuild.
We **continue to pray** for those who have lost loved ones and for everyone whose home or property has been damaged. May God give them strength as they begin the difficult road to recovery.
**Thank you for standing with our fellow Texans.**

—Mark “Tex” TeixeiraRepublican Nominee for the 21st Congressional District of Texas

[**FIRST**](https://link.email.mikerogersforsenate.), during my first run for Senate, I was a longtime Congressman with little to no name ID. This cycle, I will be entering the race as an established candidate who earned the support of nearly 2.7 million Michiganders.
| | 2

[**SECOND**](https://link.email.mikerogersforsenate.), President Trump's victory in my state was a watershed moment. Michigan was long seen as a key pillar to the “blue wall” – in other words, a state that consistently votes Democratic. We're entering the midterms with an entirely different landscape.
| | 3

[**THIRD**](https://link.email.mikerogersforsenate.), the Democrats are already running with their tail between their legs. Gary Peters, our incumbent Senator, decided he would rather quit his job than face me in a race he was sure he would lose.
[ HELP ME FLIP MICHIGAN RED ](https://link.email.mikerogersforsenate.)
This open race is a Republican's best chance to flip a Michigan seat since 1994, Friend. If I'm going to win, I will need a top-notch team by my side and it would mean the world if you would join me. I'm ready to get to work on day one and be a man you will be proud to call Michigan's next Senator.

| | We're officially halfway through 2026, and before Congress breaks for the August district work period, I wanted to share a quick update on what we've accomplished, what we're still fighting for, and what's ahead. I'll be candid: governing has become increasingly difficult under an administration that too often creates chaos instead of solutions. But even under these circumstances, my team and I continue to deliver for El Paso. **What We Accomplished** We focused our energy where El Pasoans need it most: securing our fair share of federal resources to grow our local economy and protect our families. As a member of the House Appropriations Committee, I fought hard during the recent budget markup to secure $45 million directly for El Paso. But the real reward is seeing those federal dollars come home and go to work for our community. Last month, I was out in El Paso celebrating major new investments, including presenting $1.031 million in Community Project Funding to El Paso Makes to bring local manufacturers together to spearhead high-tech defense-aerospace production right here at home. We also secured two major safety infrastructure investments totaling $4.8 million to protect our neighborhoods from severe weather. This includes nearly $1 million to improve flood alerts for families and emergency responders, alongside $3.8 million to upgrade critical stormwater mitigation for Central El Paso. These projects save lives, and even under gridlocked conditions, we are proving that we can deliver real improvements back home. Earlier this month, I voted for the bipartisan _21st Century ROAD to Housing Act_ , and now it is law. The new law takes meaningful steps to address our nation's housing affordability crisis by helping increase housing supply, limiting corporate investors from buying up single-family homes, and creating more opportunities for working families to achieve homeownership. **What's Ahead** When Congress returns, I'll continue fighting for the priorities I hear most from El Pasoans: _lowering daily costs, strengthening border communities, supporting our veterans, and protecting our democratic institutions_. But before we return to Washington, I'll spend the coming weeks doing one of the most important parts of this job: listening. I will be meeting with constituents, local organizations, small business owners, educators, veterans, and community leaders throughout our district. These conversations shape my work and ensure that the voices of El Pasoans remain at the center of every decision I make. There is still much work ahead, but I remain optimistic because I know the strength, resilience, and determination of the community I have the privilege of representing. clean_body: From securing federal funding for El Paso to fighting for accountability in Washington. | | | | We're officially halfway through 2026, and before Congress breaks for the August district work period, I wanted to share a quick update on what we've accomplished, what we're still fighting for, and what's ahead. I'll be candid: governing has become increasingly difficult under an administration that too often creates chaos instead of solutions. But even under these circumstances, my team and I continue to deliver for El Paso. What We Accomplished We focused our energy where El Pasoans need it most: securing our fair share of federal resources to grow our local economy and protect our families. As a member of the House Appropriations Committee, I fought hard during the recent budget markup to secure $45 million directly for El Paso. But the real reward is seeing those federal dollars come home and go to work for our community. Last month, I was out in El Paso celebrating major new investments, including presenting $1.031 million in Community Project Funding to El Paso Makes to bring local manufacturers together to spearhead high-tech defense-aerospace production right here at home. We also secured two major safety infrastructure investments totaling $4.8 million to protect our neighborhoods from severe weather. This includes nearly $1 million to improve flood alerts for families and emergency responders, alongside $3.8 million to upgrade critical stormwater mitigation for Central El Paso. These projects save lives, and even under gridlocked conditions, we are proving that we can deliver real improvements back home. Earlier this month, I voted for the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act , and now it is law. The new law takes meaningful steps to address our nation's housing affordability crisis by helping increase housing supply, limiting corporate investors from buying up single-family homes, and creating more opportunities for working families to achieve homeownership. What's Ahead When Congress returns, I'll continue fighting for the priorities I hear most from El Pasoans: lowering daily costs, strengthening border communities, supporting our veterans, and protecting our democratic institutions. But before we return to Washington, I'll spend the coming weeks doing one of the most important parts of this job: listening. I will be meeting with constituents, local organizations, small business owners, educators, veterans, and community leaders throughout our district. These conversations shape my work and ensure that the voices of El Pasoans remain at the center of every decision I make. There is still much work ahead, but I remain optimistic because I know the strength, resilience, and determination of the community I have the privilege of representing. = Thank you for allowing me to be your voice in Congress. I'll keep fighting for you every single day. With gratitude, Veronica | Donate Today If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Veronica Escobar instantly: | = | = | = | = ---|---|---|--- | | | Paid for by Veronica Escobar for Congress. |

Las Cruces Mayor Ken Miyagishima is OUT of the governor's race — and he endorsed Republican Gregg Hull on his way off the ballot. Sounds like great news for Hull, right? Not so fast.

Plus: the Rubio speech that had Krysty thinking of Reagan, and the coming split in the Republican Party nobody's talking about yet.

Trump's own teleprompter operator is under federal investigation for making over $100K on prediction markets using early access to presidential speeches — and that's not even the wildest story in this Wall Street Journal report. It's insider trading with a new coat of paint, and it's just getting started.

$50,000 short, and time is running out
Displaced children with nowhere to turn are exactly who traffickers target.

| | | | [](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=739cf0298df04c9faef2e142c1b5f60b&_e=csLAFh-kwXdQ-MB8NXiAzyAKt9KKsbolvg_un3ar9zlNhg93ncxaIxj8SMEsgCUry-WqaA1wRAsGYP6Wu3rr0fDYBMmPJEAl60Eh_T6On68YFLLWLHtnyypQyfzvQx5LtVMtLuxlbRBI_EuZBzlR1cvrs0ZrwM6OSGx4p6HSn8kNg6jiqdzIlzhSjKXcu0d57xW-wH8UrxO2xNBYI7iBlhHg7zReS9gvq4Mezw7Xd9onZ_zGJe0UJ9YQrDzVascDc-95tOegDYEeDIondTbngANirXcnjXcPF7K_r16C4dJjMe_C_sjcxfp8HrgZ9rzrpjcqAV2sHMgyC0_GCsb82Lj_tlbs3fA4uECC2xcfWZ9ylIfDzbb4cHAlXvv6pni7g4MjJ23ik8bfbkHJkBQ5_VzJ4CaL36eWgK4RJ46JUFTNj5bFPu6gRLZXywSOrZaaLJMWghdYexw5BhvT_B79VUXKZ9_8LOm7PhmMJqUTIiBwWLeTEjT7C3ywH1zVJJu7cBuTWC22yQrgtxE426PSEKDK6n6lmJyS-LgE_uu1tcbdt9NIzNijHlL7tMtJtr6CSi22xNTHlX4MWJQ8P0RM9OLBFAsNfKGpTUCZbNsxUDRqX65r3uM04fa52LQ-onsgCaUqIocLzefuA_kjkRqG77tsV6qiBN7T7euPX9MSHvTCXnZcfwu8rZzPvEelsLsm)
---
| |
---
| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Peter, A child who survived the earthquake in Venezuela may have lost everything else.Their parents. Their home. Every relative who might have taken them in. Now they have nowhere to sleep, nothing to eat, and no one left to protect them.**When a child has nowhere to turn, someone else will offer to take her somewhere.** **Too often, that someone is a trafficker, and they know exactly how to make the offer sound like help. **
---
[](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=739cf0298df04c9faef2e142c1b5f60b&_e=csLAFh-kwXdQ-MB8NXiAzyAKt9KKsbolvg_un3ar9zlNhg93ncxaIxj8SMEsgCUry-WqaA1wRAsGYP6Wu3rr0fDYBMmPJEAl60Eh_T6On68YFLLWLHtnyypQyfzvQx5LtVMtLuxlbRBI_EuZBzlR1cvrs0ZrwM6OSGx4p6HSn8kNg6jiqdzIlzhSjKXcu0d57xW-wH8UrxO2xNBYI7iBlhHg7zReS9gvq4Mezw7Xd9onZ_zGJe0UJ9YQrDzVascD0DybPw-xZ-PlQIS6OQcz95PAVuRuUPbv65cQ8qRQP2yKMGnUFqJXGfN5gPnLE3J2xEy9K8v_6FsNkXL-hx17fbhYA083Pvq-VfH_W6D0IAaaHBLrUi6GYDmhA7QMnO9_q11n3NixF-J8ZjC7_6rvU4hpGyHw5jF9-jmgXLuUugY3Wag4lV17iCLSKWYxK5ehDcMeLQHWkaJ7P2M_xKtYr1HjE3a1Ate4-iQrUcEfYvll1z65Y5BFisaqXNqX7FAWzGBSa1AXUGDmfJphT0Tgwf5z2daYwv6X7KAvSH2ztY1heGS-PiD__raOGQ7rDHQGvX6b3lnjx43j-bi5Pzl-lkOdZ_LXew2O7Vb9_GoywDEybfZwtGH-K0YuTEIEUpSOpJyal9crAVoS_adbLm-KfEeZihTNkBr25juUzISkOUfkexWrkW4HTGKI-5xi49Yu)
---
They study the gaps left behind by disaster, and they move quickly, often faster than the systems built to protect children can respond. A shelter without enough staff. A registration process that hasn't caught up. A crowd of frightened families too overwhelmed to watch every child closely. These are the openings traffickers are trained to find.
---
[ Give Before It's Too Late](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=739cf0298df04c9faef2e142c1b5f60b&_e=csLAFh-kwXdQ-MB8NXiAzyAKt9KKsbolvg_un3ar9zlNhg93ncxaIxj8SMEsgCUry-WqaA1wRAsGYP6Wu3rr0fDYBMmPJEAl60Eh_T6On68YFLLWLHtnyypQyfzvQx5LtVMtLuxlbRBI_EuZBzlR1cvrs0ZrwM6OSGx4p6HSn8kNg6jiqdzIlzhSjKXcu0d57xW-wH8UrxO2xNBYI7iBlhHg7zReS9gvq4Mezw7Xd9onZ_zGJe0UJ9YQrDzVascDLhJiiIf3WuZrZ93mlr0_L5hPp-56b7wsBCE950T0JjCZRF_ej2LaV5gS26hXLa8HIxPo-Elkj2PnLGdV8kuILdFBLlrBIrmN_CoL3hGHf5y0tyc6v5hYgOZE9vBEFXTOTDqPaVCGLqybVl06ybgau2apR2TztL7db9t_l8JHWBScO2xmul_fokP5TOv9caGy-F1Ie3BXhKO-n2K7kfeKnYaleCDykTYwRiVdZClCYvFgIn-zs0SGLh81GLjnq_ql_NzPCfLVLLNkLEkZ0Eb-6asqW3DG1tzw1iqFnkeu6kkmFP3zBDkuQaTEv3dgvsPXqkNylTAUGKncWKFX9-C22_GvPjQ7x9bOK9v2_YQ8qLU-l8o9T_9OVFGHIe63yRRGjOGL-ydiJiEqibt1fiZME7ZfIG9BfQFt9cS0kUUxHhwNKSWMIiQnIRzDL4pKc59t)
---
My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the film Sound of Freedom, and founded the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** because I believe, without reservation, that every child deserves to be safe, and **none of them are for sale.** Right now, we are working urgently with organizations on the ground in Venezuela. We are helping so that displaced children what they need most: food, water, and a safe place to be found before a trafficker finds them first.
---
[](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=739cf0298df04c9faef2e142c1b5f60b&_e=csLAFh-kwXdQ-MB8NXiAzyAKt9KKsbolvg_un3ar9zlNhg93ncxaIxj8SMEsgCUry-WqaA1wRAsGYP6Wu3rr0fDYBMmPJEAl60Eh_T6On68YFLLWLHtnyypQyfzvQx5LtVMtLuxlbRBI_EuZBzlR1cvrs0ZrwM6OSGx4p6HSn8kNg6jiqdzIlzhSjKXcu0d57xW-wH8UrxO2xNBYI7iBlhHg7zReS9gvq4Mezw7Xd9onZ_zGJe0UJ9YQrDzVascDNE606oqLQC-6CKDN6aDh1Qqsx7MjG3lTx1Z_dwtxlosD8qg4bMFW6-ce6QhH283OJ0BlrpgvVnJYGWp70-YkImjDdRRj-bjP9gYyuqDB7nQGiwScWEfHApWhFrGD3BZf8RvpPuk2gkOfzcuzHcImHMtdhMXWR41hOq7QdeRinbi-QbtiNS_tL4y4OOSjsFE-6kqotKD-321uIUBikXN4mrsD595k97I5RLofexX3itBCf3O-sGSqN3r26K53gThF_Mx5S6JDc3UpE-zJtxJYAguNoVWXnu5yT87MMEwD36V45F2Nkvt8P304bY9Qg49LmtWY9_y98VXXKOWArc0uHRU4aMjzLEXbRvXRHHdhGMs9xHoaX5IpXHPkWb74fMYtnYvb6Fnjzn8aO4wb9oi39HEVFkcWYTQcukiRL1oy1WFgZsElnPVpAaGzi6x8IZ1I)
---
A simple meal or a safe shelter can be the difference between a child staying protected and a child disappearing into a trafficking network. **This work depends on partners we trust deeply, and on donors willing to help fund what those partners cannot do alone. ****Every dollar helps close a gap a trafficker would otherwise use. **We are also funding direct efforts to stop the traffickers themselves, before they can take another child. Their home. Every relative who might have taken them in. Now they have nowhere to sleep, nothing to eat, and no one left to protect them.When a child has nowhere to turn, someone else will offer to take her somewhere. Too often, that someone is a trafficker, and they know exactly how to make the offer sound like help. They study the gaps left behind by disaster, and they move quickly, often faster than the systems built to protect children can respond. A shelter without enough staff. A registration process that hasn't caught up. A crowd of frightened families too overwhelmed to watch every child closely. These are the openings traffickers are trained to find. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the film Sound of Freedom, and founded the Sound of Freedom Foundation because I believe, without reservation, that every child deserves to be safe, and none of them are for sale. Right now, we are working urgently with organizations on the ground in Venezuela. We are helping so that displaced children what they need most: food, water, and a safe place to be found before a trafficker finds them first. A simple meal or a safe shelter can be the difference between a child staying protected and a child disappearing into a trafficking network. This work depends on partners we trust deeply, and on donors willing to help fund what those partners cannot do alone. Every dollar helps close a gap a trafficker would otherwise use. We are also funding direct efforts to stop the traffickers themselves, before they can take another child. Iran Kills Two More U.S. Troops
Iran's war with the United States turned deadlier over the weekend, with [three Americans](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLuunTAQAL8GOiN7eZnCRZrT3bQp0YIX2BuDkddAzt9H5xduOc2MNH--xi_kwMf6G3dyLDL66EfBm3DOPuGOsl3Zx-dYeN3yCBo6pXsFesQ5801jg6V3LRi72JKc6W3TDqbtTbm5uSMk03fWDDCZyXgC3Q11V3sLhrAv2X18ugcNdQutrizYTjeWpmXyEwx10ejr9Jip4kPYk8wxnmcMnHmWKqa1DG7L-ZSi_lXAq4DX8zzVEv8d9Eg1x72AV-Cb1IcLeF2iOOGhHkyK0zoricEzJVGeMG8qUcbAmGN6K8mJ_5Ko75g8Hur7Cm9lhjI5fz4cAkvXF41ed-TwKZX5p_tuB_8DAAD__4p9g8U) killed in ballistic-missile and drone strikes on bases in Jordan and Iraq. The Pentagon on Monday [identified two soldiers](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2unTAQxfHVmM7IHj5fQZGG7qVNiQbbwLxrbMQM19uPbpaQ8jTnJ_3_fC_fSJHS_hvPMBHz4rNfGN8BnfgbT-TjEZ9L2mg_ZAEDvTaDBrOgE3qHpcXKTx3YcRurMNlhbLsv2w22Oibcmm11vhl6B_3qu3XsETewaFdrx8FWNH3-zAAGmg46U48w9qYdw7qtfoWvRrXmuTxKqCkx-cAu5-vKkYQc1_neqzgdIher5peCWcFcSqkL8kFpl5yEzsC1y6eCOYXCCuaPqGD-eeK_oWC-QhLcc9LkQxLaKLCWkvXDmnP0FG7WL4oxeE03JsKkUQTdS__k22PSK3JQMFf35K9CMRL3g2rNfiLFD17J_5Z9T_A3AAD__8dwjHQ) — a 25-year-old lieutenant and a 19-year-old private — with a third service member's remains still being examined. President Trump vowed fresh retaliatory strikes honoring the fallen, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared Iran had effectively killed the deal keeping the Strait of Hormuz open. Tehran's chief negotiator, meanwhile, [chastised Washington](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LvOnTAQBOCnMZ2RWe4FRRq6P21KtMc2sJEvhF2OlbePTh7hL2eK-aT59bV9IQVKx0-MfiHmzWW3Mb49WnE3RuTzEZdL2uk4ZQMDgzajBrOhFXr7rcPKLT000z5VfmnGqevnph-b6lxagL3DebCNgdfQTziiGcHYHVszzPNQ0fLZ-3TQ9tCbeoJpMN3kX_vLvWBuVWeey6H4mhKT82xzvq4cSMhyne-jCsspcrFqfyhYFayllLogn5QOyUkoeq5tjgrW5AsrWD-igvX3E_4HBSvdmFjbk_yukz-yEEq-tT2RhdizfljH_KZ06OSLjhRI8P6r_Z-HruiTKFire3FXoRCIh1F15ohI4QNX8t1X3wv8CwAA__9YqopF) for surging new military equipment into the region while professing to seek peace.

★★★
Gas Tops $4 Again
The Iran war is hitting Americans at the pump. The national average for regular gasoline [climbed above $4](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0L3OnDAQheGrMZ2RGX7sLVykofvSpkSz9hhmBTZivMvtR5tLSHma95HOn5_lB3nnvP7GgzyLLLHERfBDGGq88EDZ3jWWOydet7qAgUkbq8EsGCp_aBmwiX6EziXXkO-sG8ZHN9qu2fyU0KCbqEthCNGmwfTOGhenh-0NxtSw__aMBQP9CKNpHbjJDI6e6Rmf8OjVYN5nxEotZ-FIEko5z7Jz5SBtudZm91utp6j-l4JZwXzfd3ujbJzXWnLlg6QN5VAwZ7pFwfwVFcyv9_5vKJhXFH1eHEj0xUJ60PihC1fSiS-p-hvRwjmQPjjq1zuTgrm5fDxv3neWyarBrAfy_qWa-r8_fjz8DQAA__8pI4R2) a gallon Monday for the first time since mid-June, up from $3.87 a week earlier, as turmoil around the Strait of Hormuz disrupts global oil flows. Brent crude traded above $80 a barrel. [The symbolic threshold](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D-ynDAMgPHTmM6MreXfFhRp6F7alIzWFqAE2wwSS3L7zF7hXeD7zXy_vuYv5J3z-hMTjSwyxxJnwTdh0HhiQtkujeXOC6-bzuCgs6634GYMym-aG6zi2IIflqGi0fdD0z592_tqG5E8tW23vJwPEMPDx466HrrmSb4NS1_x-Om5Hhw8WmhdPcDQuWag1_KKL3g-TOOuI6JSzVk4koRSjqPsrBykLuda7eOmeoh5_DAwGZju-65vlI3zqiUrJ5I6lGRgynSLgekjGph-X7uByQ8GJj4xW8F_YuWSg3LkvNpQUmJNlFUsZ6WTk42Eu73E6l0s_Q0b5pUsqmL48ylX5xiPm_edpetN49aEvH_wSr979j3C_wAAAP__hLKMdQ) adds political pressure on Republicans ahead of the midterms, after prices had eased following a first-stage deal that since collapsed. Iran suspended its commitments under that interim agreement last week, and the [national average](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D1uhDAQxfHT2J2RGTBmCxdp6DZtSjT-AEYxGGEvzvGjVW6Q8jU_6f2_nvMTKdKxfuIeDOU8--TnjHdAV_yFO-btVXyqx0LrVmaQMAipBcgZXaE7zD1ybxS04zLyYFo99urRKt3yzVjpFw_WgnJa2wd46dGFgJ1aoGsVcjJvT2qQ0ClQshlhHGQ_BrtYb-HRsV6-To8lNHRk8iG7lM4zRSrkcpOulUezlXJm1n0wmBhMtdZmST9HqLlxaWcwRbqDeG8G0ysLuvAQFS-Ry0XfIf-9ETDwy_izUoyUB816ue5I8W3w8t8wt4HfAAAA__8ifXTk) now sits well above year-ago levels near $3.14. ★★★
U.S. Exits Iraq
After 23 years, American forces are set to leave Iraq by Sept. 30, winding down a mission that began in 2003. But security experts warn the withdrawal could open a vacuum, with one counterterrorism researcher cautioning that ISIS is [actively waiting](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LEOnDAQBNCvgc7IGIO5wkWa6y5tSuSzF1jJYMe7nC9_H6H8Qdop3mjm12t5OYx4bj_dARaJlpDCQu4DznMo7nC0XxxSPVfcdl6UVJOQRii5OM_4gUW7NthR9fM6t2B7M-vx0Y-mb3erBgNmUqE3Uptp9mGUQRsP0zCsk-x1i_b2pFFSDaMaZTereZJ6hvf6Dm_1GBotrxwcQ4cnYQDyKeWcIjJ66lLZ2mh35kzN8KNRz0Y9a63dmr4nVOp8Ou4klRga9URCEjkhQRDwzTEhix2JU0EvLhJY3G8BX2TBUEoqYivpyuLfzPhHVIeM5yY2l-kGoLCorpzUFhtyxRiRJtNouR0O413e8v8--rHqbwAAAP__pJyLhg) to exploit the gaps as the U.S. departs. President Trump [announced the timeline](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckDuOpTAQAE8DmZHdfGwCB5uQvU03RA1uoCWDWdvAvNuPXjAXmLxUJdW_1_hC9nysf3EnyymNLrgx4U04Zxdxx7Rd2YXnWHjd8ggSOiG1ADninPmmscHS2RaUWUxJVmnTtL1qtSo3S7pblHFS91q5aWr7pjVLB46U1qCgK9l-fFKDhLqFVlYGTCcbQ9MyuQn6umjkdTrMVPGR2FGaQzjP4DnznKoQ19LbLeczFfWfAoYChud5qiV8HfSkag57AcMPXsCQ47WfItJN6JN4NjrElcTOnjPGt_CENwmO-F_gkikKqMWbMIqdU-JwlNG682HvOXW6aOS6I_tPpcy_XXdb-A4AAP__PUOCDw) alongside Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, arguing Iran has been weakened enough for Baghdad's forces to stand alone. The move comes as the broader war grinds on — a conflict [fought largely](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0E3upCAQQPHT4A6D1X7gwsVs3PVsZ2lKKLAmCAawzdx-0lf4X-D9kvfnvb2RA0f_G09auJTNJrsV_BCaajOeWI672vREx_6oGygYpZokqA1N5Q9tPTZ2GaDTTje0dJPuh7kbpq45Fu30OLgZ93HeASfz2l2ncTeTmcnYDhpevj01gYLXAINqNehR9Zp2t9sd5pfo1X1ZrNRyLGypmJSuKwWubEqbsm_CctR6FfH6JWAVsD7P0z5YDo6-plj5pNKadApYIz1FwPoVBax_7yBg7WYBayYXyFSOXpoUXWBTpUu3P6oMmD2FfxI5y26Sd5GF8ocNyZPOnXKRlskKWJu82OvhELiMk-iVP5HDF27qT69-FvgfAAD__5nsiqo) by air that has now claimed at least 17 U.S. service members.
GOP's Cash Ground Game

Republicans are pressing their financial edge into turnout, with Americans for Prosperity Action knocking [nearly 2 million doors](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLHOpCAURp8GOw1eQbGg2MZutt3SXIHBmwgYL6P7-JvZR_i7r_nOSc6f1_pCOijH35iCJebVF78y3gFd9Rcm5P1TfXnym-JeV5AwtnJqQa7oKt1hVdh4q6E3b9ME209G6bnXU9_sVslRSq38PGkwfW-0mqXzWsIQwoYTNmS_PDmBhEGDlp0BM0plwvbe_AbzIJT8nB5r6Cgz-cCulPMsB1Vy3JUrNofdaz1ZDL8ELAKW53m6B3mnHGvJ4S8myuHqXEkClhweFrA4TCdSzP93yfEKzFQyHgIWNep-lKOAJZazdch7e5caLm4T-Rqu9D01l_XnQ8dBPE5CyZiQjq-jqT9teFv4FwAA___DH4NS) across battleground Senate states including Iowa, Montana, North Carolina, and Michigan, leaning on a committee-cash advantage after the Supreme Court's coordinated-spending ruling.

★★★
Fetterman's Democratic Red Line

body:
“Out Gunned Under Siege”
It took me a long time to get this right

| | | | Peter, I'm going to be blunt with you, because the stakes are too high for anything less. Please read this entire message. It has taken me over an hour to write this as I collect my thoughts... **The radical Left is attempting a hostile takeover of the great state of Texas -- and they are funding it at a level that should alarm every freedom-loving American who reads these words.** _The Texas Tribune just confirmed it:**my far-left opponent, James Talarico, raised over $30 million in a single quarter**. That's more than triple what we raised._ **This is not an accident.** This is a coordinated, well-funded assault by the Democrat political machine -- the _same machine that has been working systematically_ , state by state, to dismantle the constitutional republic our Founders bled to build. They have targeted Texas because they know what we know _: if they flip this Senate seat, they flip the balance of power in Washington!_ These far-left political fanatics will spend as much as it takes. They'll flood Texas with cash to try to crush us. This is the playbook of people who do not believe in America. It is the playbook of those who hate America. **Remember:** They want wide-open borders. They want far-left control over our children's education. They want to pack the Supreme Court. They want Christianity gone. They want to silence dissent, crush opposition, and fundamentally transform this Nation into an unrecognizable nightmare, with malice towards every patriot who has ever stood and placed their hand over their heart... **They tried to destroy me with witch hunts. They failed.** **They tried to stop us in the primary. They failed.** **They raised $30 million to bury us.** **They will fail again --**_but only if you act right now!_ _**I need you to understand this**_**:** money in politics is not just money. It is air cover. It is television ads running in Houston, Dallas, and San Antonio. It is field organizers knocking on doors in precincts across this state. Every dollar they raise that we do not match is a dollar spent convincing Texans to surrender their freedoms to Washington bureaucrats and far-left globalist interests. **We have raised $9 million since April. But we must raise more to stay alive.** The path to victory -- the path to defending President Trump's Senate Majority and holding the line against the radical Left's agenda -- runs directly through your decision in the next few minutes. _Will you stand with us?_

The path to victory -- the path to defending President Trump's Senate Majority and holding the line against the radical Left's agenda -- runs directly through your decision in the next few minutes.
